candidates.content_text:
Junior Civil Drafter - Global Rail Infrastructure Team
Perth, WA | 3 months contract
About the role
An exciting opportunity has become available for a Junior Civil Drafter to join a globally connected Rail Infrastructure team based in Perth.
This position is ideal for a recent graduate or early career drafter looking to develop their technical skills and build a long-term career within a collaborative engineering environment. You'll gain exposure to major rail and civil infrastructure projects, working alongside experienced specialists delivering projects from concept through to construction across Australia and internationally.
Key Responsibilities
 - Prepare accurate 2D and 3D drawings for rail and civil infrastructure projects.
 - Develop rail alignment plans, longitudinal sections, cross-sections and track layout drawings.
 - Produce drawings for earthworks, drainage, and associated civil infrastructure.
 - Prepare Issued for Construction (IFC) documentation in line with project requirements and industry standards.
 - Manage drawing revisions and incorporate design updates throughout project delivery.
 - Maintain drawing registers and support document control processes.
 - Collaborate with multidisciplinary engineering teams to ensure quality and consistency across project deliverables.
About You
 - Certificate or Diploma in Civil Engineering Drafting or equivalent qualification.
 - Proficiency in AutoCAD and/or MicroStation.
 - Strong attention to detail and commitment to producing high-quality documentation.
 - Ability to interpret engineering drawings, standards and specifications.
 - Strong communication and teamwork skills.
 - Ability to manage multiple priorities and meet project deadlines.
About Airswift
Airswift is an international workforce solutions provider within the energy, process and infrastructure industries. Airswift serves as a strategic partner to our clients, offering a turnkey workforce solution to capture and deliver the top talent needed to complete successful projects by aligning with the unique needs of our clients.
With over 1000 employees and 9,000+ contractors operating in over 130 countries, our geographical reach and pool of talent available is unmatched in the industry and the level of experience, exposure and expertise that the organization has is unparalleled.
Only candidates with the right to work in Australia will be considered. (Australia Citizen, PR Holder, or Valid Australia working VISA)
If you would like to be considered for the position, please apply directly to this advertisement or send your application via email to kashmera.vijayakumaran@airswift.com with your updated CV/ resume & contact details. Alternatively, you may contact Kash at +61 08 6256 0338 for more information.

Join a close-knit, collaborative team where people support each other

candidates.content_text:
Kickstart Your Career in Engineering Drafting!
Ready to turn your interest in design and engineering into a career?
Whether you’re finishing Year 12, recently left school or studying Civil Drafting at TAFE, this is your opportunity to get started in the engineering industry.
STP Consultants is looking for an enthusiastic Junior Civil Draftsperson to join our growing Brisbane team. You’ll work alongside experienced civil engineers and drafters, gain hands-on experience and learn how the drawings you create become part of real projects across Queensland.
You don’t need years of experience. We’re looking for someone with the right attitude, curiosity and willingness to learn.
Why you’ll love working here
Start building your career
Get hands-on experience from day one and develop practical civil drafting skills while learning from experienced engineers and drafters.
Work on real projects
Go beyond the classroom and see how civil engineering projects come together. You’ll contribute to drawings and documentation used throughout projects from concept and design through to delivery.
Learn from experienced people
Ask questions, share ideas and learn from people who genuinely want to help you develop. You’ll receive guidance and mentoring as your skills and confidence grow.
Be part of a great team
Join a close-knit, collaborative team where people support each other, work together and enjoy what they do.
Work in Fortitude Valley
Our Brisbane office is in the heart of Fortitude Valley, close to public transport, cafés, restaurants and everything the city has to offer.
The Opportunity 
As you develop your skills, you’ll have the opportunity to:
- Assist with preparing civil drawings, plans and project documentation.
- Work with engineers and experienced drafters to produce clear, accurate and high-quality drawings.
- Learn industry standards, guidelines and best-practice drafting processes.
- Develop your understanding of how civil engineering projects are designed and delivered.
- Participate in project discussions and meetings to build your understanding of project requirements.
- Carry out basic drawing and documentation checks with guidance from experienced team members.
- Take on more responsibility as your skills and confidence develop.
About you:
You could be a great fit if you are:
- A Year 12 student, recent school leaver or currently studying Civil Drafting at TAFE.
- Genuinely interested in civil drafting, design and engineering.
- Curious and keen to learn new skills.
- Detail-oriented and take pride in producing accurate work.
- A good communicator who is comfortable asking questions and taking feedback.
- Reliable, organized and willing to have a go at new challenges.
- Someone who enjoys working with others and being part of a team.
- An Australian Citizen or Permanent Resident.
Most importantly, bring your enthusiasm and willingness to learn. We’ll help you turn it into a career.
What’s in it for you?
- 
Career development: Build your skills through hands-on experience, mentoring and ongoing professional development.
- 
Flexibility: Enjoy a 9-day fortnight, flexible working hours and the option to purchase additional leave.
- 
Competitive remuneration: A package that reflects your experience and contribution.
- 
Recognition and rewards: Employee referral rewards and recognition programs.
- 
Great culture: Work with supportive people in a friendly, collaborative environment, with regular team and social events.
- 
Wellbeing support: Access to a confidential Employee Assistance Program.
- 
Long-term opportunity: Build your career with an established, Australian-owned engineering consultancy.
About STP Consultants 
For more than 20 years, STP Consultants has been helping shape communities across Queensland. We’re a privately owned, multidisciplinary engineering consultancy, bringing together expertise across Civil, Structural, Mechanical, Electrical, Hydraulic, Fire and Seismic engineering. 
Our teams work on a diverse range of projects across Queensland, giving you the opportunity to learn from experienced professionals and see the many different paths an engineering career can take.
Our values of Potential, Respect, Integrity, Deliver and Engage shape the way we work with our clients and with each other.
We’re proud of our approachable leaders, supportive team environment and commitment to developing people and delivering quality engineering outcomes.
Ready to get started?  
If you’re looking for more than just a first job and want to build a career in engineering, we’d love to hear from you.
Click Apply and send us your Resume and Cover Letter.
In your cover letter, tell us:
1. Why you’re interested in starting a career in civil drafting.  2. What interests you about joining STP Consultants.
STP Consultants is an equal opportunity employer. We value diversity and welcome applications from all backgrounds.

candidates.content_text:
Why our People Choose Quickway
At the heart of our business are our greatest assets, our people, our culture and our core values of honesty, openness and fairness.
At Quickway, we are committed to nurturing talent and developing people. As we grow, we ensure that our people and their skills grow with us. Working with us, there are often opportunities to learn and build on your experience and we actively encourage professional development. We believe in building our people so that they can build Australia's future.
We partner with our clients and teams to deliver without compromising on our core values. We recognise and reward the efforts and achievements of our people.
Start Your Civil Engineering Career with Quickway
Quickway is a leading civil infrastructure contractor delivering projects across Roads & Bridges, Concrete Structures, Rail, Utilities, Communications, Electrical and Water Infrastructure throughout NSW and QLD.
We are seeking an enthusiastic Undergraduate Civil Engineer to join our team based at our Burleigh Waters Project in Queensland.
This opportunity is ideal for a 3rd or 4th year Civil Engineering student looking to gain practical, hands-on experience while completing their degree. Whether you are seeking your first engineering role, vocational placement or looking to gain exposure to live civil construction projects, we would love to hear from you.
No prior industry experience is required. We are looking for someone with a positive attitude, willingness to learn and genuine interest in building a career in civil engineering.
About the Role
You will be part of the project team delivering the Cassowary Drive Bridge Replacement project, which has just kicked off, and will run through to completion in the second half of 2027. The project is a $18 million infrastructure project delivering a new flood-resilient bridge and improved transport connectivity for the growing southern Gold Coast community. Working alongside experienced Project Engineers, Site Supervisors and Project Managers, you will gain exposure to all aspects of project delivery including:
- Site-based engineering and construction activities
- Quality assurance and project documentation
- Construction methodologies and planning
- Safety and environmental compliance
- Subcontractor coordination
- Site inspections and reporting
- Quantity tracking and progress monitoring
- Survey and set out activities
- Contract administration and project controls
This is a hands-on role that will provide valuable exposure to the civil construction industry while allowing you to continue your university studies.
What You Will Bring
Essential
- Currently studying a Bachelor of Civil Engineering.
- In your 3rd or 4th year of study.
- Ability to travel to our Burleigh Waters project site.
- Strong communication and interpersonal skills.
- Positive attitude and willingness to learn.
- Full working rights in Australia with the intention of pursuing a long-term career in Australia.
- A genuine interest in civil construction and infrastructure projects.
Desirable
- Current Driver's Licence.
- Previous construction, labouring or site-based experience.
- Completion of vocational placement or internship programs.
- White Card.
What We Offer
- Flexible work arrangements to support university commitments.
- Approximately 3 days per week with additional hours available during semester breaks and project requirements.
- Exposure to major civil infrastructure projects.
- Mentoring from experienced industry professionals.
- Practical experience that complements your university studies.
- Opportunity to transition into a Graduate Engineer role upon completion of your degree.
- Supportive team culture focused on learning and development.
 If you are looking to gain real-world engineering experience, work alongside experienced professionals and build a long-term career in civil construction, we would love to hear from you.   Apply now or contact Suzi Dimech at suzid@quickway.com.au for further information.
candidates.teaser: We have an exciting opportunity for an Undergraduate Engineer to join our team on the Gold Coast.

candidates.content_text:
Are you currently studying a Bachelor of Engineering (Civil) and looking to gain real-world engineering experience while you complete your degree?
Launch your engineering career with Shellharbour City Council and develop practical skills, industry knowledge and professional networks through a structured cadetship program designed to support your transition from university to the workplace.
The Civil Engineer Cadetship is a structured training and development opportunity for students who have successfully completed at least four semesters (96 credit points) of a Bachelor of Engineering (Civil) and are about to commence or are currently undertaking their third year of study.
Combining paid practical experience with ongoing study, you'll work alongside experienced engineers and professionals across Engineering, Asset Strategy and our Oak Flats Services Depot, gaining valuable exposure to a broad range of local government engineering functions.
You will have the opportunity to contribute to projects that shape the future of one of NSW's fastest growing cities. 
Gain hands-on experience across areas such as:
 - Road and transport infrastructure
 - Traffic engineering
 - Flood and stormwater management
 - Civil works and construction projects
 - Project delivery and asset planning and management
 This is an opportunity to apply what you're learning at university to real projects that make a difference in the local community.
Through Council's Cadet, Apprentice and Trainee (CAT) Program, you'll receive ongoing mentoring, professional development and on-the-job training while completing your degree. The program is designed to build future talent and support students to develop the technical, professional and leadership skills needed for a successful career.
For more information on our CAT Program, click here.
About us: 
Shellharbour City, located in the Illawarra region, is just 80 minutes south of Sydney and is home to over 86,000 people in a city that spans 154 square kilometres. It's an area of great natural beauty - stretching west from the picturesque coastline to rolling pastures, set against the majestic backdrop of the Illawarra escarpment. 
Our dedication to be financially sustainable in an evolving environment, while striving for a great organisational culture and committing to employing staff who embrace our core values, has made Shellharbour City Council an employer of choice.
We have been recognised with numerous state and national awards in recent times, including eight wins for our First Nations Community the Yirran Muru (many pathways) playspace, as well as being presented as winners in the NSW Landscape Architecture Awards, Regional Achievement Awards, and Parks and Leisure Australia Regional Awards of Excellence.
We offer:
Shellharbour City Council offers a high performing and sustainable organisation to deliver outcomes for the community through leadership, collaboration and innovation. We have exciting, rewarding career opportunities and flexible working arrangements to support a healthy work/life balance. 
 - Temporary full time, 35 hours per week with access to flexi-time 
 - Commencing salary range from $1,116.30 - $1,279.60 per week (based on university progression)
 - Plus 12% superannuation
 - Payment of course fees upon receipt of enrolment record
 - Additional Allowance of $230 per subject for essential student expenses such as administration fees, course materials including textbooks and prescribed readings
 - Study and Examination Leave for face-to-face and online courses
 - Structured Cadetship Program including a Mentor and Peer Program
 - Plus benefits including novated leasing, retail discounts, corporate fitness programs, Employee Assistance Program (EAP) support & Learning & Development opportunities
 - Plus Annual Award Increases & Bi-annual bonus payments & weekly pay run
 - Plus a range of local government benefits, including LSL after 5 years, one week 'My Leave', health & wellbeing initiatives as well as generous parental leave entitlements. 
 For further information about the position, click here for the position description.
Contact: Kristi Barrett, Team Leader Learning and Development on 4221 6236. 
Closing date: Monday, 5 October 2026 at 11:30pm. 
Apply now...

When you have submitted your application, an email confirmation will be sent to your nominated email address. Please ensure you have the correct email address and check your inbox (including your "junk" inbox). 
For further information about the selection process including tips on how to address the selection criteria, please view our Guide to Applying. 
Shellharbour City Council is an Equal Opportunity Employer and values the unique strengths and talents of all people. Aboriginal Torres Strait Islander people, people from culturally and linguistically diverse backgrounds and people with a disability are encouraged to apply.
At Shellharbour City Council we promote respect at work as a fundamental right for all and strive to create a workplace free from discrimination and harassment. This commitment extends to the promotion of the rights of all children and young people to be safe from harm when interacting with our services and spaces. Our values, Collaboration, Accountability, Integrity, Respect and Sustainability underpin all we do.

candidates.title: Junior Civil Engineer – Retaining Walls
candidates.abstract: Design and build retaining walls while developing your skills in PLAXIS, geotechnical engineering and hands-on site construction.
candidates.content_text:
Location: Sydney, NSW
Employment Type: Full-Time
We are seeking a motivated and reliable Junior Civil Engineer to join our growing construction team, specialising in retaining wall design and construction.
This is an excellent opportunity for a recent Civil Engineering graduate or junior engineer looking to develop their skills across geotechnical engineering, retaining wall design and construction, while gaining practical site experience on projects across Sydney.
About the Role
Working closely with our Project Managers, Site Supervisors and construction team, you will assist with the design, planning, coordination and delivery of retaining wall projects from commencement through to completion.
Your responsibilities will include:
- Assisting with the design and engineering of retaining walls
- Assisting with geotechnical assessments and engineering calculations
- Using PLAXIS for geotechnical modelling and analysis
- Assisting with stability analysis and retaining wall design
- Reviewing engineering drawings, plans and project specifications
- Assisting with site set-out, levels, measurements and inspections
- Monitoring construction activities and progress on site
- Assisting with design changes and technical queries during construction
- Preparing and maintaining engineering and construction documentation
- Assisting with ITPs, QA/QC documentation and project records
- Assisting with quantities, material take-offs and progress claims
- Checking construction works against approved drawings and specifications
- Liaising with project managers, supervisors, subcontractors, consultants and suppliers
- Identifying engineering and construction issues and assisting with practical solutions
- Assisting with technical documentation, reports and project correspondence
- Maintaining a strong focus on safety, quality and compliance
About You
The ideal candidate will have:
- A Civil Engineering degree or relevant qualification
- 0–3 years' experience in civil or structural construction/engineering
- A strong interest in retaining wall design and geotechnical engineering
- PLAXIS experience and an understanding of geotechnical modelling
- Knowledge of retaining wall design principles and stability analysis
- Ability to read and interpret engineering drawings and specifications
- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills
- Excellent attention to detail
- Good communication and organisational skills
- A practical understanding of construction methodologies
- Ability to work independently and as part of a construction team
- Current Australian driver's licence
- White Card
Desirable Experience
Experience or knowledge in the following will be highly regarded:
- PLAXIS 2D / PLAXIS 3D
- Geotechnical engineering
- Retaining wall design
- Soil and foundation behaviour
- Slope and global stability analysis
- Reinforced concrete retaining walls
- Cantilever and gravity retaining walls
- Temporary and permanent retaining structures
- Australian Standards and relevant engineering specifications
- Civil construction and site engineering
What We Offer
- Full-time position with an established construction company
- Hands-on experience across retaining wall design and construction
- Exposure to both engineering and construction aspects of projects
- Opportunity to develop your geotechnical and PLAXIS skills
- Mentoring and support from experienced engineering and construction professionals
- Career progression and professional development
- Variety of retaining wall projects across Sydney
- Competitive salary based on experience and qualifications
Apply Now
If you're a motivated Junior Civil Engineer looking to develop your career in retaining wall design, geotechnical engineering and construction, we'd like to hear from you.
Please submit your resume through SEEK.

candidates.content_text:
Fortec are market leaders, with a reputation for excellent technical expertise and engineered solutions. Fortec is an Australian owned contracting company that specialises in:
- Bridge Construction and Maintenance
- Marine Structures
- Post-Tensioning of Building & Civil Concrete Structures
- Specialist Engineering Services for Bridge Launching; and
- Jacking and Geotechnical Services including Ground Anchors, Soil Nailing & Micro-piling.
We are looking for a Junior Civil Engineer to join the QLD team, who has completed their studies in Brisbane, and is based in Brisbane.
About the Role 
Reporting to the Senior Project Engineer, the role splits their time between office and onsite tasks, assisting the senior engineer with project tasks. Key responsibilities will include:
- Preparing technical reports, logs and basic design specifications
- Visiting sites to inspect work quality, monitor safety compliance and gather data
- Assisting with compiling project documentation
- Effectively communicating with clients, project staff and key stakeholders
- Ensuring company quality, environmental, health and safety processes are adhered to
- Ensuring tasks are planned and prioritised, to meet budgets and deadlines
- Assisting with the onboarding of new wage staff. 
About You
Key qualifications and skills required include:
- Bachelor’s degree in civil engineering, or a related field, completed in Australia, and preferably Brisbane.
- 1-year of Australian industry experience in civil infrastructure projects, with exposure to bridge construction, maintenance, or remediation an advantage.
- Sound understanding of engineering practices.
- Ability to proactively manage tasks and priorities to ensure planned budgets and timeframes are met.
- Ability to work as part of a team and coordinate job schedules.
- Sound knowledge of relevant legal requirements, including health and safety.
- Sound communication skills, with the ability to work with people at varying levels.
- Sound organisational skills, with attention to detail and accuracy.
- Demonstrated understanding of computer packages related to the field of Civil Engineering, including the Microsoft Suite (Office, Project) and finance software.
Why Fortec……
Fortec is a reputable and well-known company and employer, who provide a range of rewarding career opportunities for individuals looking to make their mark. You'll gain practical experience across the planning, design and delivery of civil infrastructure projects, working alongside experienced engineers and project teams.
From roads, footpaths and drainage to water sensitive urban design and transport infrastructure, you'll be exposed to a diverse range of projects and challenges. You'll also build experience working with consultants, contractors and a broad range of stakeholders, giving you an understanding of the project lifecycle from concept through to delivery.

To be successful in this role you will have:
 - Graduated within approximately the last two years or are expecting to graduate within approximately the next 6 months in Civil Engineering.
 - Eligible to join Engineers Australia as a Graduate Engineer (GradIEAust) upon completion of tertiary qualification.
 - Knowledge of the principles and practice of civil engineering, and emerging trends, principles and operations with an understanding of civil engineering operations and function.

 - Ability to provide welcoming, responsive and respectful customer service to colleagues and community members, with a commitment to continuous learning, professional development and applying feedback.
 - Ability to take ownership and accountability for deliverables.
 - Skilled in communication and being able to present effectively both orally and written.
 - Strong organisational skills, the ability to successfully manage competing priorities, maintain attention to detail and meet deadlines.
Why Our Graduate Program?
Our graduate program gives you a great opportunity to start building your career, while having our genuine impact on our City and our communities. As a capital city council, we have wide-ranging responsibilities, so you'll be exposed to many different industries. This includes everything from community wellbeing to urban planning, events to infrastructure, lifestyle experiences to heritage, economic development to climate action, corporate services and many more.
Apart from gaining valuable insight into what makes our community unique, are entitled to a wide range of benefits such as:

At the City of Adelaide, we thrive in an environment that is welcoming, inclusive and safe, and celebrates difference. We value and embrace our diverse perspectives and recognise the value diversity has in fuelling innovation and enabling brilliant experiences for our diverse community.

The City of Onkaparinga is committed to a diverse, inclusive, and accessible workplace. We welcome applications from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people, individuals with disabilities. UGL and CPB Contractors are recruiting for a Civil Undergraduate Engineer to join the Humelink West Project in Wagga Wagga.
Two CIMIC Group companies, UGL and CPB have been selected by Transgrid to deliver the 130km western section of the HumeLink high voltage electricity transmission project.
HumeLink is a new 500kV transmission project which will connect Wagga Wagga, Maragle and Bannaby in regional NSW that will significantly increase the capacity of the electricity network in Australia’s eastern states. HumeLink is one of Australia’s largest energy infrastructure projects, with about 365kms of proposed new transmission lines and a range of other new and upgraded infrastructure.
The HumeLink West scope of works, worth $1.4bn, includes delivery of new 500kV double circuit transmission lines spanning 130kms from Wagga Wagga Substation to a new Substation at Gugaa, the Interface Point with HumeLink East near Gundagai and a new substation at Maragle in the Snowy Mountains for future connection to Snowy 2.0.

 - Represent and promote the business values and business whilst providing a value for money service to the business

 - Strong communication skills (oral and written) including strong negotiation and influencing skills and the ability to establish effective working relationships with a variety of people at different levels both internally and externally

candidates.title: Civil Project Engineer
candidates.abstract: Join Aurizon to deliver major rail projects and take ownership of rail infrastructure projects from concept to construction and handover.
bullets: Build your engineering career delivering complex projects across Queensland's
Hybrid role with flexibility to work both in office and from home
Work for a leading top ASX listed company that values its people
candidates.content_text:
Location: Rockhampton
Remuneration/Benefit: Industry-leading Enterprise Agreement remuneration, including overtime and penalty rate entitlements, supported by strong career development opportunities.
Aurizon is seeking a Project Engineer to join the Construction Management team within Network.
Why join our team?
- You'll work in one of the most dynamic sectors of construction. Rail closures are high-pressure, high-consequence environments where success comes from quality planning, teamwork and execution. The rewards are seeing your work delivered in real time and being part of a team trusted to keep critical freight infrastructure operating.
- Enjoy long-term stability and certainty. Unlike many project delivery roles, you'll be part of a permanent team with a predictable pipeline of work and visibility of planned projects well into the future.
- Be home most nights. This is not a FIFO or project-hopping contractor role. You'll have the opportunity to build a career while maintaining a lifestyle outside of work.
- Plan your life with confidence. Our forward work program provides visibility of major works and shutdowns, allowing you to better coordinate leave, family commitments and personal interests.
- Join a close-knit, high-performing team that supports one another and takes pride in delivering challenging projects safely and successfully.
About the Role:
In this role, you'll be responsible for managing the delivery of rail infrastructure projects across Aurizon's CQCN network, from initial customer engagement and project development through to construction and handover.
Working closely with customers, operations, maintenance teams, contractors and industry stakeholders, you'll develop project scopes, delivery strategies, programs and budgets, while providing technical leadership throughout the project lifecycle.
This is a hands-on role that combines engineering, project management and field leadership. You'll spend time both in the office and on site, overseeing construction activities, managing project risks, ensuring compliance with safety and environmental requirements, and driving project outcomes that deliver value for our customers and the business.
You'll join a highly experienced team delivering a diverse portfolio of rail infrastructure projects, offering the opportunity to take ownership of meaningful works, develop strong industry relationships and build a long-term career within Aurizon.
Other responsibilities will include but aren’t limited to: 
- Delivering asset renewal projects, maintenance and external projects covering general earthworks, formation, bridges, culverts, level crossings and other rail-associated works. 
- Provide support to project team throughout the entire project lifecycle, from tendering to project completion. 
- Collaborate with multi-disciplinary teams to identify and resolve delivery roadblocks and escalate when required. 
- Provide advice in relation to project planning and develop project cost estimates, risk assessments, development of construction methods, procedures and programs when required. 
- Managing Contractor’s safety performance, project progress, conformance with scope of work, contract deliverables, quality standards and specifications. 
- Provide support and supervision to field operations, ensuring work complies with quality, safety, environmental standards and other relevant standards and legislation and foster a culture of excellence in project outcomes. 
- Identifying design and constructability issues and assist in providing the most efficient solution. 
About you:  
- Bachelor of Engineering (Civil preferred). 
- CPEng/RPEQ qualifications (or working towards). 
- Current Class C Drivers Licence (mandatory). 
- Ideally 5 years' experience in project delivery across mid to large-scale civil projects (essential). 
- High level of skill in planning, organising, and programming of infrastructure construction projects. 
- Familiarity with WHS and Environmental legislation and ability to produce Safe Work Method Statements (SWMS), understand company Quality procedures and WHS Act. 
- Strong level of computer skills, including Microsoft and Primavera (preferred). 
- Excellent interpersonal, communication and negotiation skills both written and verbal. 
- Willing to commit to travel as needed and willing to relocate to Rockhampton for the role (NO FIFO/DIDO). 
- A self-starter with a strong work ethic, accountability and ownership mindset, who proactively drives solutions and delivers outcomes with minimal supervision.
 What we offer you:      
At Aurizon, we support the development and growth of our employees. With a national portfolio of operations, we offer long-term and exciting career opportunities. 
Some of our benefits include:
- Development and growth opportunities.
- Access to mentoring and development programs.
- Discounts on selected health insurance funds, personal travel, gyms, vehicles and retail brands.
- Parental leave program and super booster.
About Aurizon.
Aurizon is Australia’s largest rail freight operator and a top 100 ASX company. Each year, we deliver more than 250 million tonnes of Australian commodities right across the country. Aurizon is crucial to the Australian economy, connecting miners, primary producers and industry with international and domestic markets.
Look to Aurizon for a diverse and collaborative culture.
At Aurizon, we are proud of our diverse, collaborative, creative and high-performance culture. We celebrate the contribution of every employee and provide opportunities for career development in a dynamic, caring, and inclusive work environment.
To learn about us and our company values, please visit www.aurizon.com.au/careers

candidates.title: Civil Project Engineer – TMR & Council Road Construction
candidates.abstract: Civil Project Engineer for TMR and Council road infrastructure with genuine career progression into Project Management.
bullets: $185,000 – $205,000 package + bonus scheme
Proven Track Record of Developing Engineers into PMs
No-Ego Culture | High Staff Retention
screening_questions: Which of the following statements best describes your right to work in Australia?
candidates.content_text:
Civil Project Engineer – TMR & Council Road Construction
- TMR & Council Road Infrastructure
- Proven Track Record of Developing Engineers into PMs
- Long-Term Secured Pipeline Across Brisbane / SEQ
- No-Ego Culture | High Staff Retention
- Two Project Bonus / Performance Schemes
- $185,000 – $205,000 package + bonus scheme
If your goal is to become a Project Manager, you need more than another Project Engineer title on your CV. You need exposure to the full job. You need to understand the program, the dollars, the subcontractors, the client, the methodology and what is actually happening out on site — not spend the next three years buried in QA paperwork.
That’s where this opportunity is different.
Empower Management has been retained by a well-established Queensland civil contractor delivering TMR and Council road infrastructure across Brisbane and South East Queensland. Importantly, this business has a genuine track record of developing Project Engineers into Senior Project Engineers and Project Managers. They actively look for switched-on engineers who want responsibility, want to understand how a project makes money and want to eventually run their own jobs.
If that is where you want your career to go, this is worth a conversation.
You’ll work across a strong pipeline of civil infrastructure including:
- TMR and Council Road upgrades
- Pavements and roadworks
- Bulk and detailed earthworks
- Stormwater and drainage
- Structures and bridges
- Services and utilities
- Concrete and associated civil works
- Traffic staging and live-environment construction
These aren’t roles where you get pigeonholed into one small section of a major project.
You’ll get exposure across the full delivery cycle and work closely with experienced Project Managers, Supervisors and construction teams.
As Project Engineer, you’ll have genuine ownership across both the technical and commercial side of project delivery.
Your responsibilities will include:
- Supporting the Project Manager with overall project delivery, programming and commercial performance
- Developing and monitoring short-term construction programs and look-aheads
- Coordinating Supervisors, subcontractors, suppliers and site resources
- Managing RFIs, ITPs, lot records, hold points, QA documentation and technical submissions
- Reviewing drawings, specifications and TMR / Council requirements
- Assisting with construction methodologies, sequencing and temporary works planning
- Monitoring quantities, productivity, labour and plant performance
- Tracking project costs, forecasts and cost-to-complete
- Assisting with procurement, subcontract packages and supplier negotiations
- Managing variations, delays, contractual notices and supporting commercial claims
- Reviewing subcontractor progress claims and performance
- Identifying project risks and commercial opportunities early
- Coordinating client, consultant and stakeholder requirements
- Supporting monthly reporting, forecasting and project financial reviews
- Driving safety, quality and environmental compliance across your work areas
The expectation is that you get involved.
Ask questions. Understand the numbers. Get out on site. Work with the Supervisors. Understand why the methodology works — or doesn’t. That is how this contractor develops its future Project Managers. They Want Engineers Who Are Going Somewhere
This isn’t aimed at someone who simply wants another PE job. The client is specifically interested in engineers who are focused, commercially aware and ambitious about progressing into project management.
You’ll suit the business if you:
- Want to progress toward Senior Project Engineer and Project Manager
- Take ownership rather than waiting to be told what to do
- Understand that good engineering needs to work commercially as well as technically
- Enjoy being involved with construction teams and solving problems on site
- Can communicate comfortably with Supervisors, subcontractors, clients and management
- Raise issues early and bring solutions with you
- Want to learn how the entire project operates, not just your own section
- Are competitive about performance without bringing the ego with it
- You don’t need to know everything already.
- You do need to be hungry to learn it.
The business has built a strong reputation for retaining and developing its people.
A number of its senior delivery people have progressed internally, which is exactly the pathway they want to continue creating for the next generation of engineers.
You’ll receive:
- Direct mentoring from experienced Project Managers and senior leaders
- A clear individual development pathway
- Exposure across technical, operational and commercial project delivery
- Genuine opportunities to take on more responsibility as you prove yourself
- Strong project pipeline across Brisbane and SEQ
- Competitive salary package
- Two project-based bonus/performance schemes
- Family-friendly environment
- A practical, low-politics culture where good people are backed
There’s no interest here in keeping a capable engineer in the same box for five years.
If you perform, you’ll get more responsibility.
What You’ll Bring
- Civil Engineering degree or equivalent
- Around 4-5+ years of civil construction experience
·        TMR experience will obviously be highly regarded, but equally important is your attitude toward development and taking responsibility.
- Good understanding of civil construction methodology
- Working knowledge of QA, ITPs, RFIs, programming and project documentation
- Exposure to cost control, procurement and subcontractor management
- Ability to read drawings, specifications and project contracts
- Strong communication skills with both site and client-facing teams
- A practical, solutions-focused approach
- Genuine ambition to progress into project management
This is a smart move for a Project Engineer
seeking stability, challenge, broad experience and genuine career momentum in a
high-value, low-politics environment.
Interested? Apply today via the link or connect with us directly at jobs@empowermanagement.com.au
candidates.teaser: Civil Project Engineer for TMR and Council road infrastructure with genuine career progression into Project Management.

Why You’ll Love Working With Us
At the City of Vincent, we’re driven by our vision to be courageous, clever and creative – bold in our ideas and deeply connected to our community. We’re committed to making a difference by delivering high-quality services that improve the lives of our residents.
This isn’t just a job; it’s a career with real benefits:

The role involves preparing construction drawings using AutoCAD and other design software, undertaking site investigations and inspections, assisting with project feasibility assessments.
Working alongside experienced engineering professionals, this is an excellent opportunity to develop your technical skills, gain exposure to a broad range of local government infrastructure projects and build a rewarding career in engineering design.

Thank you for your interest in joining Team Vincent.

bullets: Get a head start on your engineering career
Rotate across Planning, Design, Delivery, Maintenance and Operations

candidates.content_text:
- Part Time Fixed Term | 16 hours per week 
 - Commencing February 2027
 - Position Overview - Undergraduate Position Brief 
 If you are heading into the final year of your engineering degree, our 2027 Undergraduate Academy gives you the opportunity to gain practical industry experience while completing your studies.
 Over 12 months, you will work alongside experienced engineers on real projects that help shape, build and connect the Gold Coast, developing practical skills, building industry connections and exploring where a career with the City could take you.
 Start your career at the City
 Starting February 2027, the Undergraduate Academy is designed specifically for students entering their final year of university. You will work 16 hours per week during university study periods, giving you the flexibility to balance your studies with meaningful professional experience, with opportunities to increase your working hours during university breaks.
 This is an opportunity to take what you are learning in the classroom and see how it is applied in the real world, contributing to projects, working with experienced professionals and developing practical engineering capability before you graduate.
 What’s on offer
 As an Undergraduate Engineer, you will complete a planned 12-month rotational pathway across the engineering asset lifecycle, gaining experience across Planning, Design, Delivery, Maintenance and Operations.
 Through a combination of Core and Micro Rotations, you will experience different stages of the asset lifecycle, work across a variety of engineering teams and projects and build a broader understanding of engineering at the City. Your rotational pathway will consider your engineering discipline, individual interests and the opportunities available across the City, giving you broad and purposeful experience across the lifecycle.
 Throughout the program, you will be supported by a dedicated Mentor, providing guidance and continuity across your 12 months and a Rotation Leader within each placement to support your day-to-day work and development.
 Who can apply?
 Our Undergraduate Engineer opportunity welcomes students completing a Bachelor of Engineering in Civil, Structural, Environmental, Electrical, Mechanical or Process Engineering. To be considered for this opportunity you must:
 - be enrolled in and entering the final year of a relevant undergraduate Bachelor of Engineering degree at a recognised Australian university when the program commences, with approximately 12 months of study remaining
 - have Australian citizenship, permanent residency or a visa with appropriate working rights for the required hours and duration of the program
 - be available to work 16 hours per week during university study periods
 - be available to work in person at City of Gold Coast workplaces and locations
 - be able to obtain a Construction White Card and meet relevant WHS requirements
 Apply Now!

In your cover letter, tell us about your engineering studies, career interests, work experience, volunteering or extracurricular activities and the areas of engineering you are most interested in exploring. Most importantly, tell us what you hope to learn by putting your university studies into practice with the City.

candidates.title: Project Engineer – Civil / Structural – Transmission

candidates.content_text:
Project Engineer – Civil / Structural (Transmission Infrastructure)
 If you're a Civil or Structural Project Engineer with experience delivering transmission, utilities, energy, mining or major infrastructure projects and enjoy being at the forefront of construction delivery, this could be an excellent opportunity to join a significant energy infrastructure project in Western Australia.
 NES Fircroft is partnering with a leading infrastructure organisation delivering a major transmission project in regional WA. Due to ongoing project requirements, we are seeking an experienced Project Engineer to support the successful delivery of critical civil and structural works associated with new transmission infrastructure and network connections.
 Job Title: Project Engineer – Civil / Structural (Transmission Infrastructure)
 Location: Approximately 2 hours from Perth 
 Salary: Circa $150,000 - $160,000 package depending on experience
 Length: Fixed-Term Contract
 Roster: Monday to Friday, Site Based
 Accommodation: Provided 
 Additional Benefits: Daily site allowance
 The Role
 This is a hands-on project delivery role where you'll be embedded within a live construction environment, supporting the delivery of transmission infrastructure works from construction through to completion.
 Working closely with project managers, contractors, consultants and engineering teams, you'll be responsible for coordinating technical activities, managing construction interfaces, resolving engineering issues and ensuring work is delivered safely, efficiently and in accordance with project requirements.
 The role is ideally suited to an engineer who enjoys a strong site presence and can effectively bridge the gap between design and construction teams.
 Key Responsibilities
- Provide civil and structural engineering support throughout project construction activities.
- Support the delivery of transmission infrastructure and associated civil works.
- Review engineering drawings, specifications and technical documentation.
- Conduct site inspections and construction verification activities.
- Ensure works are completed in accordance with approved designs, specifications and relevant standards.
- Manage RFIs, technical queries, engineering changes and contractor submissions.
- Support QA/QC processes, inspections, documentation and project close-out activities.
- Identify and resolve construction and engineering challenges on site.
- Coordinate activities between contractors, consultants, designers and project teams.
- Monitor construction progress, identify project risks and assist with mitigation strategies.
- Support commissioning, handover and defect management activities.
- Promote strong safety and quality outcomes across the project.
Key Experience
- Degree qualified in Civil Engineering, Structural Engineering or a related discipline.
- Minimum 5 years' experience in a Project Engineer, Site Engineer or similar position.
- Strong site-based construction experience.
- Experience delivering civil and structural infrastructure projects.
- Previous exposure to transmission, utilities, renewable energy, mining or major infrastructure projects.
- Experience reviewing drawings, specifications and construction documentation.
- Demonstrated experience managing RFIs, technical queries and engineering changes.
- Strong stakeholder management and communication skills.
- Practical, proactive and solutions-focused approach to engineering challenges.
- Ability to operate effectively within a fast-paced construction environment.
Highly Regarded Experience
- Transmission line construction projects.
- Overhead powerline infrastructure.
- Tower foundations, structural installations and associated civil works.
- Transmission line stringing activities.
- Substation or grid connection projects.
- Renewable energy developments.
- Utility or network infrastructure projects.
- EPC or EPCM project environments.
- Experience working to Australian standards and network requirements.
Why This Role?
 This opportunity offers the chance to play a key role in the delivery of critical energy infrastructure while gaining exposure to a large-scale transmission project in Western Australia.
 You'll join a project-focused team delivering essential infrastructure in a collaborative environment where engineering input and practical problem solving are highly valued.
 Additional benefits include:
- Site accommodation provided for the duration of the assignment.
- Daily site allowance.
- Exposure to major transmission and energy infrastructure projects.
- Long-term project involvement with strong delivery teams.
- Opportunity to work across both technical and construction interfaces.
Apply
 If this Project Engineer opportunity sounds like the right next step in your career, apply now or get in touch for a confidential discussion.
 All enquiries handled discreetly.
 With over 90 years' combined experience, NES Fircroft (NES) is proud to be the world's leading engineering staffing provider spanning the Oil & Gas, Power & Renewables, Chemicals, Construction & Infrastructure, Life Sciences, Mining and Manufacturing sectors worldwide. candidates.content_text:
Structural Draftsperson (Revit) · North Lakes, QLD · Hybrid (2 days in office)
- North Lakes, Brisbane QLD, Australia
- Full-time or part-time
- Hybrid: typically 2 days in the office, the rest at home or the office, your choice
- $85k – $105k + super, based on experience
One month you're detailing a low-to-medium rise residential tower, the next it's an industrial park, a fire station or a mine-site steel frame.
We're a small, close-knit structural engineering consultancy based in North Lakes, and we're after a structural draftsperson who wants genuine variety and real ownership of their work.
What you'll draft
- Multi-residential towers – low to medium rise apartment buildings and townhouse developments, from preliminary layouts through to full construction documentation
- Industrial and commercial – warehouses, industrial parks and steel-framed buildings, with the connection detailing that goes with them
- Community and civic buildings – fire stations, PCYCs, indoor sports centres and education facilities
- Retail, mixed-use and hospitality – projects where structure, services and architecture all have to work together
- Mining and resources – steel frames, skids and support structures for industrial clients
- Residential – new homes, house raises, extensions, decks and pools: quick-turnaround jobs that keep the week moving
You'll work in Revit across the full project – general notes, footing and framing plans, sections and details – and your name goes on the drawing sets.
What you'll need
- 2+ years hands-on Revit experience
- The confidence to work autonomously and own your deadlines
- Queensland based, able to be in our North Lakes office around 2 days a week
- Australian citizenship or permanent residents only
Full-time or part-time – your call
We're open to either. Choose a full-time role, or tell us the part-time hours that suit you, whether that's 3 or 4 days a week or shorter days around school pick-ups or study. We'll work the role around what you need. Part-time hours are pro-rata on the same salary range, and the hybrid setup still applies: part of your week in the North Lakes office, the rest at home or the office, your choice.
What we offer
- Real hybrid flexibility – typically 2 days a week in the North Lakes office working alongside the team. The rest of the week is yours: work from home or come into the office, whatever suits you.
- A proper setup in both places – you'll get a laptop that moves with you, plus a docking station set up at your home and one at the office. Just plug in and pick up where you left off, wherever you're working that day. Current Revit licences included.
- Variety you won't get at a big firm – residential, commercial, industrial, civic and mining work, often in the same month
- Ownership – you'll run drawing sets from start to issue, not just pick up redlines on someone else's model
- Career growth – room to take on more responsibility as the practice grows, with training and CPD support
- Northside location – our North Lakes office means no CBD commute
- A team that knows each other – small crew, regular catch-ups and annual team events, including our EOFY dinner
To apply, send your CV and a few sample drawing sheets (PDF is fine) to admin@skyhookengineering.com.au.

Earn and learn!
We are currently offering a traineeship which combines structured training with paid employment – allowing you to gain hands-on experience and practical skills in a real-world work environment.
About the role:
The position of Trainees Entry Level General Hand will carry out a variety of civil engineering tasks, as requested by Engineering Supervisors, associated with the general construction and maintenance of roads, drains, footpaths and other engineering assets within the City and successfully obtaining a qualification in Civil Construction. The position is for a 3-year fixed term contract period to support the learning required to complete a Certificate III in Civil Construction and most of the time will be spent gaining on the job experience. There is a requirement of attending TAFE as part of gaining the qualification. There may be further opportunities within the City of Swan once the traineeship has been completed.  
Key Accountabilities include, but are not limited to: 
 - Comply with relevant Occupational Safety and Health legislation and complete all work in a safe and efficient manner, having regard to own safety, the public and that of other workers
 - Operate and maintain all associated plant in accordance with Safe Working Practices, City policy and procedures
 - Successfully complete the requirements of Certificate III in Civil Construction and Plant Operation 
 - Carry out a variety of civil engineering tasks as requested by Engineering Supervisors, associated with the general construction and maintenance of roads, drains, footpaths and other engineering assets
 - Ensure that developed procedures and guidelines are followed
 - Provide feedback in toolbox meetings to correct quality deviations and/or faults
For more information about the role please refer to the position description. 
The successful candidate will have the following: 
 - Willingness and commitment to complete a Certificate III in Civil Construction 
 - C Class Driver’s Licence 
 - White Card
 - A friendly and positive can-do attitude, with a willingness to learn
 - Interest in developing knowledge in maintenance and construction
 - Interest in developing Work, Health and Safety (WHS) knowledge and practices
About working with us:
The salary for this position will be from $71,763.15 - $72,717.31 per annum (includes loading), depending on the skills and experience of the successful applicant. 
You will also enjoy benefits including:
 - More flexibility to enjoy a work life balance with a 9-day fortnight
 - Excellent leave entitlements e.g. purchase additional leave, Local Government public holiday
 - Generous Superannuation contributions up to a total combined 18.75% 
 - Comprehensive employee wellness program
 - Free parking options available
 - Travelsmart allowance to support public transport use or cycling to work
About the City:
The City of Swan, located north east of Perth, is the largest local government by land size in the Perth metropolitan area, and has one of the fastest growing populations. 
The City covers an area of 1,042 square kilometres, equivalent to almost 20 per cent of the Perth metropolitan area. A beautifully diverse expanse of land, the City is rich in natural assets, including the iconic Swan River and internationally renowned Swan Valley viticulture region established in 1829. Our location, services and facilities make the City an attractive place to live. The population across our 42 suburbs stands at 168,334 in 2023, but is set to reach 300,000 by 2050. 
The Whadjuk people of the Noongar Nation have been the traditional custodians of the land for more than 40,000 years. The Derbal Yerrigan (Swan River) holds enormous cultural significance for the Noongar people. The City is also rich in European history, and our community is a melting pot of multiculturalism, with one in three people being born overseas and one in five speaking a language other than English at home. Our ideal location, significant history, diverse community and strong economy ensures a positive future for the City of Swan, full of opportunity.
Our purpose at the City is to improve the quality of life for all of the people who live in, work in and visit the City of Swan by delivering our vision of ‘one city, diverse people, culture and places’ through shared values of respect, excellence, accountability and leadership. 
At the City of Swan we are committed to recruiting and retaining the right people and creating a great place to work.  We offer our employees real careers, real impact, and real rewards. 
We welcome everyone exactly as they are. We welcome people with diverse skills, experiences, perspectives, and backgrounds and encourage applications from Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander peoples, people who identify as LGBTIQA+, people with disabilities, people with a culturally and linguistically diverse background, and people of all ages. 
For a confidential discussion, please contact Revender directly on (08) 9267 9387.
For queries regarding the application process, please contact our friendly People Services team on (08) 9267 9014.
To apply please submit a cover letter of no more than 1 page that outlines your qualifications and experience and why you would be a good fit for this role, and a resume via the link.  
Closing Date: Sunday 11 October 2026 at 11pm AWST. 
The City of Swan reserves the right to commence shortlisting and interviews earlier than the closing date. The City also reserves the right to close the vacancy early. Therefore, if you are interested in applying for this position please do so as soon as possible. 
*No agencies please.

Who Are CPP? 
CPP is a leading high-voltage infrastructure provider, connecting renewable energy projects to Australia’s electricity grid. 
As a member of Quanta Services, a Fortune 500 company ranked #192 on the NYSX, we specialise in the design, construction, commissioning, and maintenance of substations, transmission lines, wind farms, and battery storage systems.
Established in 1996, we’ve connected more wind farms and renewable batteries than any other company. With over 800 employees and offices in Adelaide, Melbourne, Sydney, Brisbane, and Perth, we partner with Australia’s major transmission providers to deliver innovative, end-to-end solutions.
Join us in shaping the future of energy.
Design & Engineering
CPP has the largest in-house design and engineering team of any contractor in Australia, with over 170 specialists across Electrical Primary and Secondary, Civil, Structural, and SCADA disciplines. We provide end-to-end engineering solutions for high-voltage infrastructure, including nationally significant transmission projects, HV substations, wind farms and battery storage systems that drive Australia’s renewable energy transition.
Our engineers work closely with construction and operations teams, ensuring designs are practical, constructible, and continually refined through real-world feedback. With a commitment to innovation and excellence, we deliver solutions that support a stable, reliable, and sustainable energy future.
The Opportunity 
We’re expanding our civil design engineering capability and are looking for an Engineer - Civil to join CPP’s highly experienced in-house national design and engineering team. If you’re passionate about civil design and want to develop your career while contributing to renewable energy infrastructure, this is an opportunity to work on complex, nationally significant projects.
Working closely with our Senior and Principal Engineers, you’ll undertake civil engineering design tasks from the definition of client requirements and initial planning through to the development of concept and Issued for Construction designs. Your work will support the delivery of practical and safe civil solutions for high-voltage substations, battery storage systems and renewable energy projects.
You’ll contribute across a range of civil design elements, including stormwater drainage, bulk earthworks, pavements and access roads. Working as part of a multidisciplinary team of engineers, project managers and construction professionals, you’ll help ensure designs are accurate, constructible, compliant and aligned with project requirements.
About You

 - A degree in Civil Engineering or an equivalent qualification, with professional engineering registration highly regarded
 - At least three years’ experience in civil design, ideally within the energy, utilities, mining or major infrastructure sectors
 - Practical experience in civil design areas such as bulk earthworks, stormwater drainage, pavements and access roads
 - Experience preparing engineering drawings, design reports and construction specifications
 - Experience using AutoCAD and 3D bulk earthworks modelling software such as 12d
 - Experience with stormwater catchment and drainage modelling software such as DRAINS or HEC-RAS
 - Whilst not essential, experience in high-voltage substations, utility grid connections or multidisciplinary renewable energy projects will be highly regarded
Be rewarded at CPP. 
At CPP, we value our people above all else. We’re dedicated to investing in and developing your talent to help you reach your full potential. By joining us, you’ll have the opportunity to work on industry-leading projects and access the latest technologies. We foster a culture of innovation and welcome fresh ideas – if you're ready to challenge the status quo, we want you to be part of our team.
Benefits include:
 - Above-market salary package with annual reviews
 - Annual bonus, discretionary based on individual and business performance
 - We offer flexible working options, with the ability to work from home
 - Access to study assistance for continuous development, and a strong focus on internal promotions to help you grow within 
 - 16 weeks paid primary parental leave and 6 weeks paid secondary parental leave
 - Up to 2 weeks of purchased leave
 - We actively invest in AI capability, providing access to premium AI subscriptions to help you work smarter, solve complex problems and deliver better outcomes 
 - Choice between an iPhone or Samsung mobile & design specked engineering laptop and software 
 - Generous employee referral program up to $4,000
 - Access to an extensive benefits and discounts program with savings at over 400 retailers
 - Free Employee Assistance Program for you and your family, supporting physical, mental, and financial wellbeing

For further information, please reach out to amoritz@conpower.com.au however applications will not be accepted via email.

This is an opportunity to broaden your technical experience, contribute to meaningful projects and play an important role in the continued development of our Brisbane office.
Why you’ll love working here 
A growing team with exciting opportunities
Be part of a supportive team where your experience, ideas and contribution are valued. As our Brisbane office expands, you'll have the opportunity to build strong professional relationships, share your knowledge and make a meaningful contribution to our continued success.
Variety that builds your experience

Take ownership of your career

What's in it for you? 
- 
Competitive remuneration: A package that reflects your experience and the value you bring. 
- 
Flexibility: 9-day fortnight, flexible hours, plus the option to purchase additional leave. 
- 
Professional development: CPD support, mentoring and opportunities to build your technical expertise.

Inclusive, friendly culture: Supportive colleagues, collaborative working relationships and regular social events.

Career growth: Opportunities to take ownership of your work, develop your skills and progress within STP.

- Design roads, drainage, earthworks and flexible and rigid pavements

Civil Project Engineer
- Opportunity to work with Rio Tinto
- Ongoing assignment via Chandler Macleod
- Safety-first culture with supportive teams
 About the Opportunity
Rio Tinto is a global mining and materials company operating in 35 countries, producing the materials essential to modern life. Their operations are built on safety, innovation, inclusion and creating value for communities, customers and shareholders.
Chandler Macleod is seeking an experienced Civil Project Engineer to join Rio Tinto’s One Gladstone Self-Perform team, supporting annual wall raise programs across QAL and Yarwun. You will play a key role in the safe planning and delivery of sustaining capital civil and earthworks projects while working closely with project, construction and operational teams.
Key Responsibilities
- Support the planning and execution of annual wall raise programs.
- Manage civil work packages through the full project lifecycle.
- Coordinate engineering, procurement, construction and specialist resources.
- Monitor project schedules, budgets, forecasts and construction performance.
- Provide field engineering support and resolve technical delivery challenges.
- Manage project risks, design changes, technical queries and change control.
- Support procurement, contract administration, reporting and capital governance requirements.
- Work closely with Operations, Engineering and Construction teams to achieve safe and successful project outcomes.
About You
- Delivery-focused Civil Project Engineer with hands-on civil construction and earthworks experience; this is not a structural design-focused role.
- Bachelor's degree in Civil Engineering (or equivalent) with eligibility for professional engineering registration.
- 8+ years' experience delivering civil earthworks and infrastructure projects within mining, resources, heavy industry or major infrastructure environments.
- Strong project controls, field engineering, stakeholder engagement and EPC coordination capability.
- Demonstrated commitment to safety, quality and successful project delivery.
- Current residence in the Gladstone region is essential. FIFO arrangements and relocation assistance are not available for this role.
- Current Australian driver's licence and ability to pass pre-employment medical testing. SAP, Microsoft Project or self-perform delivery experience is highly regarded.
Why Join Chandler Macleod?
Chandler Macleod is one of Australia’s most experienced workforce partners. You’ll receive a competitive pay rate paid weekly, superannuation on all hours worked, access to our Employee Assistance Program, support from a dedicated Chandler-Rio Tinto team, simple digital onboarding, and access to future Rio Tinto assignments.
Apply Now!
Ready to take the next step? Apply today to join Chandler Macleod for an exciting onsite assignment with Rio Tinto.
At Chandler Macleod, we are committed to fostering a diverse workforce where everyone is welcome. We encourage applications from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, women, neurodiverse people, people living with disability and the LGBTIQA+ community. You can read more about our commitment to diversity and inclusion at https://www.chandlermacleod.com/diversity-and-inclusion.

You'll influence how projects are built. You'll work alongside Project Managers, engineers and site teams to shape methodology, sequencing, staging and programs. Your thinking on how to build it smarter becomes our competitive edge.
You'll work on projects worth talking about. Major mining and civil works for Tier 1 clients, across multiple states, with no two jobs the same.

- The ability to interpret drawings, specifications and contract documents under deadline pressure

- Hold a degree in Construction Management, Engineering, Quantity Surveying or similar

Junior Estimators ready for their next step are encouraged to apply. If you've got the foundations and the drive, we'll back your growth.
What's in it for you- Competitive salary package [adding a salary range here will noticeably lift applications]

McConnell Dowell is assembling our delivery team for the recently awarded Kwinana Freeway Widening Project – one of Western Australia's most significant transport infrastructure projects.

The project includes complex civil, structural, utilities and intelligent transport systems works, providing a unique opportunity to work across multiple disciplines while contributing to a project that will become a standout achievement on any engineer's CV. We are seeking experienced Site Engineers who thrive in complex construction environments and enjoy working closely with supervisors, subcontractors, designers and client stakeholders to safely deliver quality outcomes.
 About the Role
 Reporting to the Project Engineer, you will support the planning, coordination and delivery of construction activities across a diverse scope of works. You will be involved in day-to-day site operations, subcontractor management, quality assurance, cost control, programme coordination and stakeholder engagement.
 This is a hands-on project delivery role suited to engineers who enjoy being in the field and solving real-world construction challenges.
We Are Interested in Engineers With Experience In:
Civil and Structural Infrastructure
 - Road construction and freeway upgrades
 - Piling and foundation works
 - Bridge construction works
 - Retaining structures and structural concrete
 - Noise walls and associated civil works
 - Drainage and pavement construction
 Utilities
 - Electrical reticulation and power services
 - Communications and fibre optic networks
 - Utility relocations, service coordination and new services
 Electrical & Intelligent Transport Systems (ITS)
 - Street lighting infrastructure
 - Integration of roadside electrical infrastructure
 - ITS installations, including CCTV systems
 - Traffic monitoring and communications systems 
 What You'll Bring
 - Tertiary qualification in Civil Engineering or a related discipline.
 - Experience delivering major civil, transport, utilities or infrastructure projects.
 - Strong understanding of construction methodologies, drawings, specifications and site-based delivery.
 - Proven ability to coordinate subcontractors, stakeholders and multiple work fronts.
 - Commitment to safety, quality and collaborative project outcomes, supported by strong communication skills.
 About Us
 McConnell Dowell – Creative Construction 
 Our purpose is Providing a Better Life. We do that through delivering projects that connect, support and sustain communities, and through providing career opportunities that challenge, reward and grow our people. 
 From remote major resources and energy projects to city-shaping transport and water infrastructure, we have constructed thousands of high-quality, complex projects for our customers and communities over more than 60 years, in Australia, New Zealand, the Pacific Islands and Southeast Asia.
 Why join us?
 The work you’ll do will have a tangible positive impact on people’s lives, including yours. The diversity of our projects, roles and locations means greater development opportunities. We invest in our people to set and reach personal and professional goals and we have some of the best mentoring minds in the business to help you do that.  Because when you grow, we all grow.
 McConnell Dowell actively seeks and celebrates diversity, inclusion, and individuality. In a culture low on ego and high on support, we encourage everyone to make an impact. We're big enough to take on community-shaping projects, but agile enough for you to have an influence on how we do things.
 So, join us, be you, and help us create better together. Apply now!
 We are an equal opportunity employer. People of all ages, abilities, sexual orientation, gender identities & cultures including Aboriginal, and Torres Strait Islanders are strongly encouraged to apply.
 Please note all successful applicants must hold valid work rights for Australia and pass a satisfactory pre-employment medical which includes drug and alcohol checks.

Start: ASAP
Roster: METRO - Monday to Friday typically with some weekends.
We are seeking an experienced Project Engineer with a strong background in formwork, reinforcement and concrete (FRP) works. Previous experience delivering marine civil construction projects is highly desirable.
The successful candidate will support the planning and delivery of structural concrete works while managing procurement, quality documentation, cost tracking, subcontractors and day-to-day engineering requirements.
Key Responsibilities
- Plan and coordinate formwork, reinforcement and concrete construction activities.
- Prepare work packs, construction methodologies, lift plans and task-specific documentation.
- Review drawings, specifications and technical requirements.
- Raise RFIs and technical queries and assist with resolving design and constructability issues.
- Coordinate procurement of reinforcement, formwork, concrete, cast-in items and other project materials.
- Develop and maintain procurement schedules and monitor long-lead items.
- Prepare and manage ITPs, ITRs, checklists, lot records and concrete pour documentation.
- Coordinate inspections, hold points, survey requirements and material testing.
- Manage concrete pour planning, including pre-pour inspections, delivery coordination and post-pour records.
- Track labour, plant, materials, subcontractor costs and project productivity.
- Assist with forecasting, budget reviews, cost-to-complete reporting and progress claims.
- Coordinate subcontractors, suppliers, supervisors and site crews.
- Monitor construction progress against the program and identify potential delays or constraints.
- Assist with variations, quantity tracking and commercial documentation.
- Maintain accurate project records and contribute to handover and completion documentation.
- Ensure all works comply with project safety, environmental and quality requirements.
About You
- Degree-qualified Civil or Structural Engineer.
- Previous Project Engineer experience within civil construction.
- Strong practical experience delivering FRP or structural concrete works.
- Marine civil construction experience is highly regarded.
- Sound understanding of formwork systems, reinforcement installation, concrete placement and curing requirements.
- Experience managing procurement, QA documentation and project cost tracking.
- Ability to interpret engineering drawings, specifications and construction tolerances.
- Strong planning, organisational and communication skills.
- Commercially aware with good attention to quantities, productivity and costs.
- Able to work closely with supervisors and construction crews in a site-based environment.
- Strong commitment to safety, quality and successful project delivery.
Desirable Experience
- Marine structures, wharves, jetties, bridgeworks or port infrastructure.
- Pile caps, headstocks, deck slabs, abutments and other reinforced concrete structures.
- Working around tides, marine access constraints and over-water construction activities.
- Concrete durability requirements for marine environments.
- Temporary works, falsework and complex formwork systems.
- Survey coordination and dimensional control.
- Managing subcontractor packages and supplier interfaces.
To apply, please submit your resume through SEEK outlining your FRP, project engineering and marine civil construction experience.

candidates.abstract: CAD and estimating role with a growing steel pipe processing business. Work on some of the most capable profiling equipment in the country.
bullets: Work in CAD every day, building and modifying models rather than just reading dr
Early-career candidates genuinely encouraged. Support for further study

How many years' experience do you have as a CAD Draftsperson?
