Based at our Geelong Refinery in Corio, Victoria
candidates.content_text:
Company Description
Do amazing work 
A career with Viva Energy is more than just a job. It’s a chance to join a group of people dedicated to supporting Australia’s evolving energy and convenience needs. We’re a leading retail, industrial and energy business, and we’ve been helping Australians reach their destination for more than 120 years.  
Our plans for the future support Australia’s energy transition to sustainable, lower carbon energy solutions.  Through our acquisitions of Coles Express and OTR, we provide Australians with outstanding convenience. 
At the heart of our plans is people power. People who want to grow and evolve with us. People with new perspectives, energy and passion to drive Viva Energy and their careers forward.
We are seeking an experienced Engineering Draftsperson to join us for a 1-year Fixed Term Contract.
Job Description
Reporting to the Drawing Systems Controller, the Engineering Draftsperson will provide multi-disciplinary drafting support across the Geelong Refinery.
The role will primarily focus on reducing the backlog of operational drawing revisions, including updating drawings from approved redline mark-ups, field-verified information and engineering inputs.
The role may also support project drawing updates as required.
This is a contract position based predominantly on site at the Geelong Refinery.  Regular site attendance is required to undertake field verification, clarify drawing mark-ups and work directly with refinery personnel. Some remote work may be accommodated where appropriate.
Key Responsibilities
- Deliver drafting services across process, safety, mechanical, piping, instrumentation, electrical, civil and site layout drawings.
- Produce, revise and maintain high-quality 2D engineering drawings using AutoCAD and raster editing tools.
- Update controlled drawings from approved redline mark-ups, field information and engineering inputs.
- Review mark-ups and clarify incomplete or conflicting information with engineers, technicians and drawing originators.
- Conduct site inspections and field verification to confirm existing plant conditions.
- Support the as-building of operational changes, MOCs and project work.
- Ensure drawings comply with company procedures, engineering standards and drawing conventions.
- Progress drawings through the required checking, approval, revision control and release processes.
- Support document control activities and maintain accurate drawing records within Lunr.
- Provide progress updates and raise issues that may affect priorities or completion.
Qualifications
About You
You will be an experienced Draftsperson who is comfortable working across multiple engineering disciplines in a complex brownfield industrial environment.
You will have strong technical drafting skills, sound attention to detail and the confidence to identify and clarify incomplete or inconsistent information. You will also be comfortable working on site and engaging directly with engineers, technicians, Operations, Maintenance and project personnel.
You Will Bring
- At least five years of multi-disciplinary engineering drafting experience ideally in refining, petrochemical, oil and gas or another heavy industrial environment.
- Proficiency in AutoCAD and AutoCAD Raster Design, or equivalent raster editing software.
- Experience updating drawings from redline mark-ups and verified field information.
- Experience with electrical and instrumentation drawings, with P&ID experience highly regarded.
- Experience working in brownfield and hazardous-area facilities.
- Knowledge of engineering drawing standards, revision control and as-building processes.
- Experience using an Electronic Document Management System such as Lunr.
- Strong attention to detail and a commitment to drawing accuracy and quality.
- Good communication skills and the ability to work effectively across multiple disciplines.
- Ability and willingness to work predominantly on site at the Geelong Refinery.
Additional Information
About Viva Energy 
Join a team that values diversity. Viva Energy is a great place to be yourself. We believe in our people, trust in their positive intentions, and empower everyone to amplify their voice across the business. We value inclusion because that’s how we get the best outcomes. 
Awarded the WGEA Employer of Choice for Gender Equality for the past five years highlights that we are driven by our people and continuing our focus on making Viva Energy reflect the ever-changing face of Australia.  
We welcome applicants from diverse backgrounds including Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people and encourage and support diversity in our traditional and non-traditional roles.
At Viva Energy Australia, we believe flexibility is the new normal. We are open to flexibility options including hybrid, part-time, job-share and flexibility in start and finish times. We are happy to explore what this could look like for you during the recruitment process. 
Please note: This role is being sourced through Viva Energy Australia, therefore we will not be accepting applications via external recruitment agencies.
Only applications from candidates holding full working rights for employment in Australia will be considered.
Applications close Wednesday, 7 October 2026

Since establishing in Australia in 2020, FCC Construction Australia is committed to expanding the capability of the Australian construction market by leveraging our proven integration approach and demonstrating our reputation for solving complex infrastructure challenges through our innovative solutions. 
We draw on our global position as one of the top construction companies globally, operating in over 30 countries for the past 125 years and responsible for delivering some of the largest, most complex, and highly acclaimed projects globally under an integrated business model. 
Our activities span all areas of engineering and construction – we are a world leader in successfully delivering civil works and transport infrastructure - roads, railways, airports, hydraulic and marine works, tunnels, bridges – as well as residential and non-residential buildings - hospitals, football stadiums, museums and corporate offices. Currently we’re in the top 30 construction companies globally.
FCC Construction Australia has been selected as the principal Contractor on Queensland’s largest ever social and affordable housing project. The Project will be the largest modular building development constructed in Australia to date.
*Please note this role is based out of our Cairns project site office (located at Woree) and is not a FIFO role*
The Role:
To support in the delivery of our Cairns-based project, we are seeking an experienced and energetic Site and Project Engineers to jump on board.
More specifically your role scope will cover; 
- HSE: Promote safe work practices, participate in safety meetings, identify site risks and support HSE compliance and documentation.
- Site & Technical Delivery: Coordinate day-to-day site activities, review drawings and specifications, resolve technical issues and support construction delivery.
- Scope & Change Management: Monitor project scope, identify changes and variations, manage RFIs and provide technical input to minimise scope creep.
- Subcontractors & Procurement: Coordinate subcontractors and suppliers, support procurement, assess performance and assist with claims and commercial matters.
- Programme & Quality: Monitor progress against programme, coordinate works and interfaces, and ensure construction meets project quality requirements.
- Cost, Risk & Project Controls: Monitor costs, quantities and progress, identify risks and opportunities, maintain project records and support forecasting and reporting.
- Stakeholder Management: Liaise with clients, consultants, subcontractors and internal teams, coordinate meetings and maintain clear project communication.
- Project Support: Provide technical and project management support to the Project Manager and contribute to the successful delivery of the project.
To value-add, it's important you have a proactive "can do" attitude and look to take the initiative to get involved with ad-hoc tasks and proactively seek additional work.
If you have the capacity and capability, this is the sort of role that will grow with you and continue to challenge you.
Competencies we're seeking:
- Bachelor’s degree in civil engineering, or project/construction management.
- 5+ years relevant construction project delivery experience; civil and/or building projects
- Have a sound understanding of typical construction specifications used in the Australian construction industry.
- Excellent stakeholder management experience.
- Valid Driver's license 
What's in it for you:
- Generous leave policies to support wellbeing, and industry leading paid parental leave  
- A competitive remuneration package, with potential for further career progression into project management 
- Access to employee assistance program for employees and families 
FCC are dedicated to fostering a gender-equitable team and cultivating a culture that mirrors the diversity of the communities we serve. Our commitment lies in establishing a workplace that prioritizes safety and respect for all team members. We actively invite applications from individuals of all ages, cultural backgrounds (including Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples), abilities, sexual orientations, and gender identities. 
If this sounds like the opportunity you’ve been waiting for, we look forward to hearing from you soon.

candidates.title: Economic Development Cadet
candidates.abstract: Work with Council's Economic Development team to support projects that help strengthen and diversify the Wollongong economy.
candidates.location: Wollongong, Wollongong, Illawarra & South Coast NSW
bullets: Term Contract: 4 Years ​
Commencing: 1 February 2027 ​
gain practical experience while contributing to economic development projects
candidates.content_text:
At Wollongong City Council, we continuously strive to create an Extraordinary Wollongong for our community. We focus on the delivery of exceptional services, infrastructure and facilities for our community. Our aim is to work toward the community's goals in the Our Wollongong Our Future Community Strategic Plan 2035. 
Wollongong is a great place to work, live and play! Together, our responsibility is to create an inclusive community where everyone is welcome, valued and belongs. Our strength is the diversity of our people.
We lead with courage, openness and curiosity and believe our employees are the key to our success. Learn more about us here.
Economic Development Cadet
Term Contract: 4 Years ​
Salary $1,189.09 per week plus superannuation ​
Qualification:​ Degree in Commerce (majoring in Economics), or Economics and Finance or related degree with a major in economics or a related field.
Commencing: 1 February 2027 ​
About the opportunity
As an Economic Development Cadet, you'll work with Council's Economic Development team to support projects that help strengthen and diversify the Wollongong economy. The team works on a range of initiatives, including supporting small businesses, attracting investment and jobs, and delivering outcomes for the Wollongong Local Government Area.
You'll gain practical experience while contributing to economic development projects, research, analysis and stakeholder engagement. This cadetship is designed for someone who has completed the equivalent of one full time year of study in Economics, Business or a related degree, and is eligible in 2027 to enter their second year of study.
​What You'll Learn​
- Economic development in a local government setting.
- Research, data analysis and trend interpretation.
- How local economies grow, change and diversify.
- Project support and coordination.
- Stakeholder engagement and communication.
- Written, visual and verbal reporting.
- Critical thinking and problem solving.
- How Council supports businesses, investment and local jobs​
What You'll Be Doing​
- Supporting economic development projects and initiatives.
- Researching and analysing economic data and trends.
- Preparing written, visual and verbal information.
- Working with teams across Council.
- Supporting engagement with internal and external stakeholders.
- Helping identify opportunities for economic growth.
- Contributing ideas and solutions to local economic issues.​
We are looking for someone who:
- 
- Has completed the equivalent of one full time year of study in a Degree in Commerce (majoring in Economics), or Economics and Finance or related degree with a major in economics or a related field and is eligible to enter their second year of study in 2027.
- Has a genuine interest in economics, business and the Wollongong economy.
- Demonstrates strong analytical, research and problem-solving skills, with the ability to interpret data and identify trends.
- Has well developed written, verbal and digital communication skills.
- Is reliable, self motivated and takes ownership of their learning and professional development.
- Works effectively as part of a team and builds positive working relationships with others.
- Has strong organisational skills and can manage competing priorities to meet deadlines.
- Adapts well to new challenges, changing priorities and different work environments.
- Demonstrates attention to detail and a commitment to producing high quality work.
- Seeks and responds positively to feedback from mentors, supervisors and colleagues.
- Has a commitment to understanding and applying Work Health and Safety principle
​Learn more about our learning pathways program and the benefits of working at council HERE​
 ​Our cadetship program provides you with:
- Learning about local government and how we contribute to our community.
- Exciting and meaningful work that has a real impact.
- Regular mentoring with your supervisor to help develop your professional skills.
- A tailored professional development plan to help you succeed and be your best.
- Valuable industry experience
- Reimbursement of enrolment fees upon successful completion of subjects
- Paid time release to attend classes or undertake distance education required for your study.
- Work laptop provided for the duration of the cadetship
- A fun, friendly and supportive work environment!
Why you'll love working at Wollongong City Council!
- True work-life balance
 We know you work hard, and we make sure that effort is rewarded with real flexibility. Our hybrid work options, flex-time, and rostered days off mean you can maintain balance while delivering great outcomes.
- Great working conditions
 Enjoy a 35-hour work week or a 9-day fortnight with a regular rostered day off (RDO).
- Career growth and recognition
- We are committed to supporting your personal and professional development. Our initiatives include a reward and recognition program, corporate learning opportunities, study assistance, and leadership development programs to help you grow and succeed.
- Generous leave provisions
 Benefit from five weeks of annual leave per year (pro rata) and access long service leave after just five years.
- Health, safety, and wellbeing
 We prioritise a safe workplace for everyone, every day, everywhere. Our wellbeing programs support mental, physical and social wellbeing of our people to be at their best and include an Employee Assistance Program, skin and hearing checks and discounted gym memberships.
- A vibrant social culture
 Join our Social Club for monthly activities, an annual trivia night, and fantastic Christmas events!
Participate and engage in meaningful work, and contribute to our extraordinary community, where together we make a difference.
For more information, click on 'Apply' to be redirected to Wollongong City Council's job vacancy page.
Applications close 11:59pm Tuesday 6 October 2026.​
We invite everyone to apply no matter your identity, you'll be welcome. We encourage applications from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, people who are culturally and linguistically diverse (CALD), people with disability and veterans.
Wollongong Council adheres to the principles of a child safe organisation and is committed to the care and protection of all children and young people in the community. 
Applicants are required to undergo a rigorous employment screening process which will include Reference, Identity and Medical History Checks, and may also include a Nationally Coordinated Criminal History Check and Working with Children Check. Employment is subject to clearance of all these checks.

candidates.content_text:
PTG Commercial Glazing is looking for an experienced an experienced estimator with a strong understanding of the commercial construction industry to join our Gold Coast team.
This is a varied role suited to someone who enjoys the commercial side of construction, building strong client relationships and being involved in projects beyond simply preparing a quote.
You’ll be involved from the initial tender stage through to project award and coordination, working across a range of projects throughout Queensland and New South Wales.
Work closely with builders, shopfitters, suppliers and our internal team to identify opportunities, secure new work and help ensure a smooth transition from estimating through to procurement, fabrication and installation.
About the Role
Your responsibilities will include:
- Reviewing architectural drawings, specifications and tender documentation
- Preparing accurate estimates, quantity take-offs, quotations and tenders for commercial glazing projects
- Completing material and labour take-offs for glass, aluminium, hardware and associated components
- Obtaining and assessing supplier and subcontractor pricing
- Reviewing project scope, inclusions, exclusions and potential commercial risks
- Preparing and submitting tenders within required deadlines
- Following up quotations and tenders with existing and prospective clients
- Building and maintaining strong relationships with builders, shopfitters, fitout companies and industry partners
- Identifying new project and sales opportunities
- Working with clients to identify suitable products, systems and solutions where required
- Assisting with project budgets, variations and cost tracking
- Coordinating awarded projects and assisting with procurement, lead times and key project milestones
- Liaising with clients, suppliers, subcontractors, site teams and internal staff throughout the project
- Maintaining accurate estimating, project and client records
About You
Ideally, you will have:
- Previous estimating experience within commercial glazing, aluminium windows and doors, shopfitting, construction or a similar industry
- A strong understanding of commercial glazing and aluminium systems
- Experience with quantity take-offs, estimating, quoting and tender preparation
- The ability to confidently read and interpret architectural drawings, specifications and technical documentation
- Strong commercial awareness with excellent attention to detail
- Confidence building relationships and communicating with builders, project managers, suppliers and clients
- A proactive approach to following up opportunities and securing work
- Strong organisation and time-management skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities
- A practical, solutions-focused approach to problem solving
- Strong computer skills, including Microsoft Excel and Office
- V6 experience highly regarded
- Experience across estimating, sales, business development or project coordination will be highly regarded
About PTG Commercial Glazing
PTG Commercial Glazing is an established Gold Coast-based commercial glazing company delivering projects across Queensland, New South Wales and interstate.
Our work spans commercial shopfronts, architectural glazing and custom glass and aluminium packages. With our own fabrication facility and experienced installation teams, we work alongside builders, shopfitters and construction companies to deliver projects from initial tender through to installation.
This is a key role within our business, offering plenty of variety, responsibility and the opportunity to develop long-term relationships within the commercial construction industry.
If you have commercial construction or glazing experience and enjoy the combination of estimating, client relationships and project coordination, we’d love to hear from you.

bullets: ASX listed company
Dynamic role
Major projects
screening_questions: Which of the following statements best describes your right to work in Australia?
What's your expected annual base salary?

candidates.content_text:
The Opportunity
We are seeking an experienced Formwork Team Leader to lead the engineering design, drafting and certification of formwork projects across Queensland.
This is a senior technical and leadership role suited to a Chartered Structural Engineer with substantial hands-on experience designing and certifying formwork, falsework and shoring systems.
You will lead a specialist engineering team while remaining actively involved in complex engineering work — reviewing project requirements, developing solutions, undertaking structural analysis, reviewing designs and providing engineering certification.
Our formwork projects regularly involve challenging geometries, significant loads, unusual support conditions and bespoke formwork arrangements. The role offers the opportunity to work on interesting, technically demanding building and civil infrastructure projects throughout Queensland.
What You’ll Be Doing
- Lead the engineering and drafting delivery of formwork projects in Queensland
- Manage, mentor and provide technical direction to engineers, designers and drafters within the team
- Design, analyse, review and certify formwork, falsework and shoring systems
- Undertake structural analysis and detailed engineering calculations for conventional and bespoke formwork arrangements
- Develop practical engineering solutions for complex site constraints, concrete pours and construction sequences
- Undertake and review FEA and frame analysis models
- Review Revit models, formwork layouts, engineering drawings and design documentation
- Ensure designs comply with applicable Australian Standards, Codes of Practice and safety-in-design requirements
- Provide technical support to project, sales and site teams
- Liaise directly with clients regarding engineering requirements and technical solutions
- Resolve complex engineering and site issues
- Review and approve engineering documentation prior to issue
- Support the technical development and mentoring of engineers and drafters within the wider engineering team
About You
The successful candidate will have:
- Chartered Professional Engineer (CPEng) status
- Degree in Civil or Structural Engineering
- Significant experience designing and certifying formwork, falsework and shoring systems – essential
- Strong structural engineering and temporary works design capability
- Professional experience using Autodesk REVIT & Autodesk AutoCAD
- Strong experience using structural analysis / FEA software such as SpaceGass, Microstran, RSTAB or Strand7
- Strong understanding of Australian structural design standards and codes of practice
- Demonstrated ability to undertake detailed structural calculations and independently verify complex designs
- Experience leading, mentoring or technically supervising engineers, designers and drafters
- Ability to develop practical solutions to unusual and technically challenging problems
Why Join Us?
This is an opportunity to take a leading technical role within a major Australian formwork and temporary works engineering business.
You will work on a broad range of interesting and challenging formwork projects, with the opportunity to influence engineering solutions from initial concept through to final certification and site delivery.
The position combines technical engineering, design and drafting coordination, project leadership and people leadership, while allowing you to remain closely involved in the complex engineering work.
We offer a competitive salary package based on experience, strong technical support and the opportunity to work with a large national engineering team.
The role is based at our Stapylton, QLD office, supporting formwork projects throughout Queensland.
If you are an experienced Chartered Structural Engineer with specialist formwork design experience and are ready to lead technically challenging projects and a high-performing engineering and drafting team, we would like to hear from you.

Start your engineering journey with one of Australia's leading infrastructure providers and grow through real project experience.
At Downer Energy & Utilities, we are looking for motivated and ambitious Graduate Engineers to join our team and contribute to delivering critical infrastructure projects across Australia and New Zealand.
As a Graduate Engineer, you will participate in a structured graduate program, with the possibility of rotating across various business functions and project environments. You will gain valuable hands on experience supporting operational, financial, programming and administrative activities while working alongside experienced industry professionals.
This role offers the opportunity to build your technical capability, develop commercial awareness and strengthen stakeholder engagement skills while contributing to projects that power and connect communities. Flexibility and mobility are essential, as project based work may require travel and relocation throughout Australia and/ or New Zealand. 
What We're Looking For
- Degree in Mechanical, Electrical or Civil Engineering, completed in 2025 or due for completion by the end of 2026
- Australian Citizenship or Permanent Residency
- Hold current driver's licence and availability to commence in February 2027
- A willingness to learn, an open mindset and a desire to build your professional career from the ground up
- Strong communication and relationship building skills
- Excellent organisational skills and attention to detail
- A collaborative approach and eagerness to learn from experienced professionals
- A proactive, self motivated attitude with a commitment to ongoing development

At Downer, we are committed to developing our people and providing meaningful career opportunities.
You will benefit from:
- Exposure to major infrastructure and utilities projects across Australia
- Mentoring and support from experienced industry professionals
- Ongoing learning and development opportunities
- Strong focus on safety, sustainability and innovation
- A supportive and collaborative team environment
- Competitive remuneration and employee benefits
- Opportunities for long term career growth within a leading infrastructure services provider 
About Energy & Utilities
Downer Energy & Utilities delivers end to end engineering, construction, maintenance and asset management services to customers across power, gas, water, telecommunications and renewable energy sectors. Our people work on some of Australia's most significant infrastructure projects, helping to build sustainable communities and support the nation's future energy needs.
At Downer, our success is driven by our people. We are committed to creating an inclusive workplace where everyone feels valued, respected and empowered to bring their whole selves to work. We encourage applications from people of all backgrounds, including Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, women, culturally diverse individuals and people with disabilities.
How to Apply
To apply for this exciting opportunity, please submit your application online including your resume and a cover letter outlining your suitability for the role.
We encourage applications from candidates who are passionate about building a career in the utilities and infrastructure sector and are committed to delivering safe and sustainable outcomes for our customers and communities.
Please note: Downer does not accept unsolicited resumes, fees or costs from recruitment agencies, search firms or third parties. Any unsolicited resumes submitted to Downer or its employees will become the property of Downer and Downer will not be liable for any associated fees.

candidates.content_text:
Building Cadet, Commercial Construction
About Echo Projects Co
Echo Projects Co is a commercial builder based in Windsor, Brisbane. We deliver commercial spaces across hospitality, retail, workplace, medical and education in South-East Queensland, from new builds to landlord upgrades and refurbishments. We're a growing business with a tight, experienced team and a strong pipeline of work. We pride ourselves on clear communication with clients, subcontractors and each other, and we expect the same from everyone on the team.
About the role
This is a genuine cadet role. You'll be one of a small group of cadets rotating through the three parts of our business: projects, site and estimating. Each rotation gives you real responsibility on live commercial projects, working alongside our project managers, site managers and estimator. By the end, you'll understand how a construction business runs from first enquiry through to handover, and you'll know where you want to take your career.
What you'll do
Projects
- Support contract administration, including progress claims, variations and correspondence
- Prepare subcontracts and scopes of works
- Run document control across live projects
- Prepare project reports
Site
- Support the site team with administration, records and coordination
- Communicate with subcontractors and suppliers
- Learn how jobs are set out, sequenced and handed over
Estimating
- Assist with tender preparation, quantities and pricing
- Help put together subcontractor quotes and tender submissions
About you
- Currently enrolled in a construction management or related degree at university (this is a requirement)
- Clear written and verbal communication; you follow things up without being chased
- Organised, reliable and keen to learn every part of the business
- Current driver's licence and reliable transport
- Around a year in construction (site, a builder's office or a trade) would be great, but it's not essential. If you're keen to learn and willing to work, we want to hear from you.
What we offer
- Flexibility around uni classes and exams
- A clear path into project management, site management or estimating
- Work directly with experienced people, not buried in a back office
- Learn alongside other cadets in a structured program
- Laptop, monthly phone allowance, uniform, boots and PPE supplied
- First aid and CPR training
- Inner city office in Windsor
How to apply
Apply with your resume and a short cover letter telling us why you want to build a career in commercial construction, and which of projects, site or estimating interests you most.

candidates.content_text:
Company Description
With over a century of heritage in Australia, BESIX Watpac is a builder deeply ingrained in the local construction landscape. We’re building what matters, with an exciting portfolio of projects across all sectors – from stadiums and venues to complex industrial facilities, hospitals and secure infrastructure, including defence. Our footprint spans Australia and New Zealand, where we continue to deliver projects that leave a lasting legacy in the communities they serve. Our people are the beating heart of what we do, and the passion they bring each day drives our success, to build the best together.
Job Description
BESIX Watpac is seeking a Graduate Engineer to join our Construction SA division on a part-time basis, working through to our graduate program which will allow you to see all facets of the construction industry including Engineering, Design, Estimating and Safety this is a fantastic opportunity for a university student to secure a role with a Top Tier building contractor.
You will take part of our BESIX Watpac Graduate and Early Career Development Program. This program aims to develop and grow our future leaders. This two-year program builds technical knowledge within the context of an on-the-job environment and provides opportunities to develop professional business and leadership skills. BESIX Watpac Graduates & Cadets gain exposure to various areas of project delivery, and come together for learning workshops, networking, and social events.
This role will be responsible for:
- Assist in preparing cost plans and tenders by reviewing project requirements, compiling tender documentation, and coordinating proposed tender lists.
- Support quality assurance and safety management processes by monitoring compliance with project standards, documenting non-conformances, and assisting with the implementation of corrective actions.
- Contribute to estimating and project controls activities through quantity take-offs, cost analysis, subcontractor scope reviews, procurement support, and the preparation of tender submissions and budget forecasts.
- Assist with general site duties, office and administration as required.
Qualifications
The incumbent in this role will require:
- Currently studying a university-level degree in Construction Management, Engineering, or a related discipline.
- Working knowledge of MS Word, MS Excel, MS Outlook and ability and willingness to learn new software packages as required.
- Proven high level of professionalism and work ethic.
- Proven track record and ongoing focus on timeliness, accuracy and punctuality.
Additional Information
Along with a competitive remuneration package and long-term career development opportunities, our employees enjoy access to the following benefits:
- Wellbeing Days - three additional leave days per year.
- Awards and Recognition Program, rewarding employees who bring our values to life.
- Access to a wellbeing program including annual skin checks and flu vaccinations.
- Instant access to Perkbox, giving you a wide variety of perks and benefits, plus curated wellbeing tools to look after your physical and mental health.
- Social events and Family Days.
At BESIX Watpac, we are committed to fostering a workplace where everyone is valued, supported and respected. By embracing all ages, gender, ethnicity, religion, sexual orientation, education and appearance, our people feel safe, empowered, and motivated to be their best.  If you’re excited about this role but don’t tick all the boxes, we encourage you to apply if you have transferable skills and believe you would be a great fit with BESIX Watpac.
Join our talented and passionate team delivering once-in-a-generation projects.
BESIX Watpac acknowledge the traditional custodians of the land on which we live and work, and pay respect to the Elders past, present and emerging.

 This is an opportunity to join a high-volume residential builder in Western Australia, backed by the strength and resources of an internationally recognised global forestry and construction group.
 You'll create new home designs, customise solutions for clients, and contribute to the ongoing development of home ranges and display homes, working closely with internal departments and key stakeholders to deliver compliant, high-quality design outcomes.
 Why consider this role?

 - Tailoring designs to meet client briefs, council regulations and site constraints while maintaining aesthetic and functional appeal

 Ready for your next move?
 If you're an experienced residential Draftsperson looking for a role where your skills and ideas can have a genuine impact, backed by the stability of an established and growing residential builder, I'd love to hear from you.

Build Your Career in a City Made for Living Well
Canberra was named the world’s best city for quality of life in the 2025 Oxford Economics Global Cities Index. With an easy commute, access to nature, great food and culture, and a genuine work-life balance, it is an ideal place to start and grow your engineering career.
About The Role
We are seeking a Graduate Engineer to join our Engineering team. This entry-level role is a great opportunity for a recent graduate to gain hands-on experience supporting the safe and efficient operation of Canberra’s light rail network.
Reporting to the Infrastructure Manager, you will support the Engineering and Maintenance team with asset management, routine duties and ad hoc tasks. Key responsibilities include:
- Supporting the Engineering and Maintenance team with assigned tasks to support the successful operation of the railway
- Assisting with infrastructure defect management, including assessment, evaluation, reporting, obtaining quotations where required, and supporting works through to completion
- Preparing checklists, reports and other documentation under the guidance of the Infrastructure Manager and Asset Engineer
- Maintaining data quality in the Enterprise Asset Management system, including investigating network faults and undertaking root-cause analysis to identify issues and support corrective actions
- Completing ad hoc tasks as required, seeking guidance where necessary and providing updates on progress or issues
- Assisting with the development and review of internal standards, procedures, work instructions and other documentation
- Building and maintaining effective working relationships with internal and external stakeholders
- Adhering to, and suggesting improvements to, CMET practices, policies and procedures
- Actively participating in ongoing engineering and maintenance activities that support CMET’s operational goals
We’re Looking For Someone Who
- Holds an undergraduate degree in Engineering (Electrical, Civil, Mechanical, Systems or a related discipline)
- Demonstrates strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to prepare reports and documentation
- Has excellent organisation, planning, reporting, problem-solving and coordination skills
- Holds a current C class driver licence
- Desirable experience or knowledge includes:
- Rail infrastructure, asset standards and contemporary asset management practices
- Maintenance environments, asset management systems, and plant and equipment fleet maintenance
- Auditing compliance, reporting procedures and processes
- Consultation, facilitation, liaison and stakeholder engagement
Who We Are
Canberra Metro Operations (CMET) is proud to operate, maintain and promote Canberra’s light rail network—delivering safe, reliable and customer-focused public transport for the ACT.
We're a diverse team committed to safety, continuous improvement and delivering exceptional customer experiences. As Canberra's light rail network continues to grow, we're strengthening the way we connect with passengers, businesses, schools and the wider community—and this role is central to that mission.
Why You’ll Love Working at CMET and Living in Canberra
- Build your career in the world’s top-ranked city for quality of life
- A collaborative culture that values people, safety and community
- Job security in a growing essential service
- Professional development and career growth opportunities
- Healthy work–life balance
- Salary packaging and novated car leasing
- Paid parental leave
- Employee Assistance Program (EAP) support services
- Employee Referral Program
- Free secure parking onsite
Ready To Apply?
Join CMET and help shape the future of public transport in Canberra. Click Apply Now and submit your updated resume and cover letter.
Due to the safety-critical nature of this role, the recruitment process will include a pre-employment Category 3 rail medical assessment, background checks, and verification of qualifications and work rights.
Applications will be reviewed as they are received, so we encourage you to apply early.
We strongly encourage applications from women and Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples.
Visit cmet.com.au to learn more about us.

candidates.content_text:
Are you passionate about the environment and interested in building a career in bush regeneration and land management?
 Based at Oak Flats Services Depot, you will gain hands on experience while working alongside experienced staff to assist with revegetation projects, weed management, habitat improvement and hazard reduction activities. 
 You will have the opportunity to develop an understanding of environmental conservation and land management practices that help protect and enhance Shellharbour's natural environment.
 Through a combination of practical workplace experience and formal training, you will complete a Certificate III in Conservation and Ecosystem Management through TAFE, developing valuable skills and experience in the restoration, regeneration and ongoing maintenance of natural areas across the city, including bushland, wetlands and environmentally sensitive sites.
 This opportunity is anticipated to commence in January 2027 and upon successful completion of the traineeship, you will have achieved a nationally recognised qualification and gained two years of practical industry experience.
 Council's Cadet, Apprentice and Trainee (CAT) Program aims to build a skilled workforce by creating employment opportunities and developing future talent. As part of the program, you'll receive ongoing training, mentoring and support from experienced professionals while completing a nationally recognised qualification and gaining valuable industry experience.
 For more information on our CAT Program, click here.
 About us: 
 Shellharbour City, located in the Illawarra region, is just 80 minutes south of Sydney and is home to over 86,000 people in a city that spans 154 square kilometres. It's an area of great natural beauty - stretching west from the picturesque coastline to rolling pastures, set against the majestic backdrop of the Illawarra escarpment. 
 Our dedication to be financially sustainable in an evolving environment, while striving for a great organisational culture and committing to employing staff who embrace our core values, has made Shellharbour City Council an employer of choice.
 We have been recognised with numerous state and national awards in recent times, including eight wins for our First Nations Community the Yirran Muru (many pathways) playspace, as well as being presented as winners in the NSW Landscape Architecture Awards, Regional Achievement Awards, and Parks and Leisure Australia Regional Awards of Excellence.
 We offer:
 Shellharbour City Council offers a high performing and sustainable organisation to deliver outcomes for the community through leadership, collaboration and innovation. We have exciting, rewarding career opportunities and flexible working arrangements to support a healthy work/life balance. 
 - Temporary full time, 38 hours per week up to 24 months (or the duration of the traineeship) with access to a 9 day fortnight
 - Salary up to $838.00 per week (based on school level achieved & years out of school with a range from $412.70 for a school leaver up to $838.00 for 5+ years out of school)
 - Plus 12% superannuation
 - On the job training
 - Compulsory course costs are paid by Council
 - Approved leave to attend TAFE
 - Plus benefits including novated leasing, retail discounts, corporate fitness programs, Employee Assistance Program (EAP) support & Learning & Development opportunities
 - Plus Annual Award Increases & Bi-annual bonus payments & weekly pay run
 - Plus a range of local government benefits, including LSL after 5 years, one week 'My Leave', health & wellbeing initiatives as well as generous parental leave entitlements. 
 For further information about the position, click here for the position description. Please note that this position is call 'Trainee Horticulture' within our organisational structure. 
 Please Note: 
 - You will need to complete a Pre-placement Medical examination
 - You will need to obtain a General Construction Induction Card (White Card) prior to commencement
 Contact: Bronwyn Anderson, Team Coordinator Bushland Management on 0439 689 349. 
 Closing date: Sunday, 18 October 2026 at 11:30pm.
 Apply now...
 Complete the application below by answering the questions, describing how your skills and experience are relevant to the position. 
 Your Resume and qualifications can be attached on the NEXT page.
 Once you start your online application, you may save and return to this later, however incomplete applications will not be considered. You may wish to prepare your responses in a word document and then COPY and PASTE into the fields below. Your Resume and qualifications can be attached on the NEXT page.
 When you have submitted your application, an email confirmation will be sent to your nominated email address. Please ensure you have the correct email address and check your inbox (including your "junk" inbox). 
For further information about the selection process including tips on how to address the selection criteria, please view our Guide to Applying. 
 Shellharbour City Council is an Equal Opportunity Employer and values the unique strengths and talents of all people. Aboriginal Torres Strait Islander people, people from culturally and linguistically diverse backgrounds and people with a disability are encouraged to apply.
 At Shellharbour City Council we promote respect at work as a fundamental right for all and strive to create a workplace free from discrimination and harassment. This commitment extends to the promotion of the rights of all children and young people to be safe from harm when interacting with our services and spaces. Our values, Collaboration, Accountability, Integrity, Respect and Sustainability underpin all we do.
 Your decision to apply for a role at Shellharbour City Council is the first step in acknowledging your alignment to our values and aspirations to create a great workplace.

Graduate Environmental Engineer/Scientist - Adelaide
The Opportunity
We are seeking passionate, curious, and motivated early-career Environmental Engineers or Scientists with an interest in geoscience/hydrogeology, to join our Contaminated Land Management team working on real-world environmental challenges. If you are ready to get hands-on experience and contribute to solving complex environmental issues this is an exciting opportunity to learn from industry experts, develop technical skills, and make a meaningful impact on environmental outcomes.
The successful applicant will have the opportunity to work on a portfolio of large and complex site assessment and remediation projects for a growing client base.
The role will involve using your technical skills and knowledge on a wide variety of projects for both private sector and government clients including:
- Executing on-ground field investigations at a range of sites in SA and interstate
- The collection of soil, sediment, soil vapour, surface and groundwater samples and the supervision of contractors.
- Assisting on geotechnical field work programs where appropriate
- Undertaking all works consistent with our safety values, systems and procedures
- Project scoping, proposal writing and fieldwork preparation
- Evaluating and interpreting field and analytical data
- Preparing scientific and technical reports
- Collaborating with broad team to help solve complex environmental issues and develop remediation programs.
 This role is offered as a full-time role and offers flexible work arrangements for the right candidate.
About you
We are seeking talented and curious engineers who want to advance their career with a global environmental consultancy. You may be a recent graduate, or perhaps you are already in the industry with a couple of years’ experience in contaminated land investigations and remediation. Either way, you will have a demonstrable passion for field-based project work including soil and groundwater sampling, contractor supervision and safety management.
 Ideally you will bring:
- A degree in environmental engineering or science, geology, or earth relevant sciences.
- Effective written and spoken communication skills and the aptitude to confidently liaise with project teams, subcontractors and clients.
- Safety leadership in the field and commitment to adopting behavioural based safety programs.
- The drive and commitment to succeed and to be a strong contributor to the growth and success of Kleinfelder in Australia.
- A full unrestricted driver’s licence.
- Ability and willingness to travel regionally and interstate.
About Us:
Kleinfelder is a global environmental consultancy with over 3,000 professionals worldwide and nearly 100 staff across Australia. Locally strong and globally connected, we deliver technical excellence with a collaborative, down-to-earth approach. Kleinfelder’s contaminated land specialists and remediation engineers have significant expertise across an extensive range of industries and market sectors.
At Kleinfelder, we believe that great careers start with great opportunities, and we recognise that our people are the foundation of our success. We provide a supportive environment where professionals can apply their skills, continue learning, and grow alongside experienced industry experts. From day one, you'll have the chance to contribute to meaningful projects, develop your technical and professional capabilities, and make a tangible impact on communities and the environment.
What we offer:
- Graduate program
- Benefits such as; Paid overtime, (as per the Kleinfelder Overtime Policy), Paid Parental Leave, Purchase extra annual leave per year, Australia day public holiday swap.
- Friendly and supportive team environment
- Flexible work arrangements available (e.g., hybrid working)
- Access to our health and wellness initiatives (e.g., Employee Assistance Program)
- Professional career and technical development programs incl, study assistance with external and internal learning
- Professional membership support.
- Opportunities to participate in Corporate Social Responsibilities (volunteering, charity community support)
- Service recognition and reward programs including bonuses
Kleinfelder prides itself with being an equal opportunity employer where we value and celebrate diversity and inclusion. We value the diverse perspectives and life experiences our people bring. We welcome and encourage applications from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, veterans and people of all backgrounds and cultures.
If this opportunity sounds like something you have been looking for, and you meet the role requirements, we encourage you to submit your application including your CV and Cover Letter outlining your suitability for the role.
We will be reviewing applications as they are received, and the role may be filled prior to the closing date (22/10/26).
To be eligible for this position you must have unrestricted full legal working rights to work in Australia.
Kleinfelder will be managing this process and applications from third party recruiters will not be accepted.

candidates.content_text:
Department: Planning and Regulation
Reports to: Manager Planning and Regulation
Salary Range: $69,855 per annum + superannuation
Build your future in building certification!
Are you interested in the building industry, legislation and how development works are assessed and regulated?
This is an opportunity to start a rewarding career in building certification while gaining practical experience and undertaking formal study. 
As Cadet Building Certifier, you’ll work closely with the Principal Certifier as part of a small, supportive team within Council’s busy Planning & Regulation team. The role offers a genuine mix of hands-on and office-based work, with approximately 40% of your time spent in the field and 60% in the office. You’ll assist with building assessments, administration, records and systems while developing the knowledge and practical skills needed to progress through the building certification pathway.
With supervision and guidance, you’ll assist the Principal Certifier with Building Code of Australia (BCA) assessments, building certification activities and supervised building inspections. You’ll learn how to interpret legislation, plans and technical information and apply requirements accurately to real-world building and development work. You’ll also work with key systems including the NSW Planning Portal and building certification programs, maintain accurate records and assist with the preparation and management of documentation. Compliance and record keeping are critical aspects of the role, including ensuring information is accurate, current and readily available to support Council’s regulatory obligations and Building Commission requirements. As you progress through your studies and achieve A4 Building Inspector registration, you’ll progressively take on greater responsibility, including conducting building inspections with increased independence, within the scope of your registration and delegated authority.
A significant part of this cadetship is study and professional development. You’ll undertake relevant training, building your knowledge and skills towards Building Inspector level and ultimately progressing towards building certifier responsibilities. This is a challenging course and will require commitment, organisation and the ability to balance study with workplace responsibilities. You’ll be supported by experienced staff as you learn, but we’re looking for someone who is prepared to take ownership of their development, ask questions, absorb new information and keep learning. Previous experience in the building or construction industry would be highly regarded, as would an understanding of building legislation, codes or technical documentation. However, attitude, reliability and a genuine passion for developing a career in building certification are equally important.
You’ll need excellent communication and people skills, with the ability to explain information clearly, confidently and accurately to colleagues, applicants, builders and members of the community. The Planning & Regulation team works in a busy environment and sometimes has to deliver difficult or unpopular information, so empathy, patience, professionalism and a calm approach are essential. You’ll be representing Council whenever you are dealing with the community or attending a site, so you’ll be well presented, approachable and professional. Strong computer skills, attention to detail, sound administration and a customer-service focus are essential.
This is a Term Contract position for the period required to complete the approved training and formal study program (up to 4 years). The cadetship includes undertaking the NVR approved Advanced Diploma of Building Surveying and progressing through Pathway 2 to obtain Building Inspector registration (formerly A4), subject to meeting the registration requirements of Building Commission NSW.
If you’re reliable, organised, curious about the building industry, comfortable learning legislation and technology, and genuinely excited about building a long-term career in certification, this cadetship could be the opportunity you’ve been looking for.
This position is located in the beautiful town of Coonabarabran, known as the Astronomy Capital of Australia, which is midway between Melbourne and Brisbane and is known for its beautiful landscape and stunning night skies. The town has medical services, excellent schools, a variety of sporting and social clubs and a thriving tourism Industry. With the nearby Warrumbungle National Park, which is also Australia’s first Dark Sky Park, there is plenty to do and explore whether you’re looking for adventure or relaxation.
Selection criteria include:
- Demonstrated commitment to work health and safety (WHS) in the workplace
- Demonstrated interest in the building industry, local government regulation or construction, and eligibility to enrol in the Advanced Diploma of Building Surveying and participate in the Pathway 2 Building Inspector registration process.
- Completion of Year 12 (or equivalent) or Year 10 plus at least two years in the workforce
- Willingness and ability to undertake the NVR approved Advanced Diploma of Building Surveying and complete the knowledge, skills, training and application requirements for Building Inspector registration through Pathway 2.
- Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to interact professionally with the public and team members
- Good computer skills, including Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, Outlook) and ability to work with other software including the NSW Planning Portal, BCS and GIS mapping systems.
- Sound organisational skills and attention to detail.
- Ability to work as part of a team and follow instructions.
- Demonstrated commitment to confidentiality and professional conduct.
- Class C driver’s licence (P plates minimum).
It is a plus if you have 
- At least 3 years’ building and construction industry experience
- White Card (General Construction Induction Certificate)
- Knowledge of the National Construction Code and other relevant legislation.
- Familiarity with interpreting construction plans and technical documents.
Why join Warrumbungle Shire Council
Warrumbungle Shire Council offers more than just a job — we provide the opportunity to build a stable, long-term career while enjoying genuine work-life balance, strong team support, and a rewarding regional lifestyle.
As part of Council, you’ll join a workplace that values professionalism, safety, collaboration, and continuous development, while supporting the essential services and infrastructure that keep our communities thriving.
Council offers a wide range of employee benefits designed to support your wellbeing, career growth, and lifestyle, including: 
- Long service leave available after 5 years
- Flexible monthly RDO
- Paid parental and concurrent parental leave
- Generous leave provisions
- Opportunities to purchase additional leave or access deferred leave arrangements
- Ongoing training, mentoring, and professional development opportunities
- Access to thousands of free online learning courses
- Weekly pay cycle
- Salary packaging options to help maximise your take-home pay
- Flexible work arrangements and hybrid work options where operationally suitable
- Employee Assistance Program (EAP) available to employees and immediate family members
- Health and wellbeing initiatives including flu vaccinations, hearing tests and skin cancer checks 
- PPE and/or a generous uniform allowance provided, depending on the role (REMOVE FOR FUNDED. Check wording for trainees)
Warrumbungle Shire is strategically positioned on the Newell Highway, a short drive from Tamworth, Mudgee and Dubbo, and just over 3 hours from Newcastle, making Warrumbungle Shire a great place to live and work. Covering an area of more than 12,000km², and with a population of nearly 10,000, Warrumbungle Shire Council is one of the larger Local Government Areas in Central West NSW, home to the townships of Coonabarabran, Coolah, Dunedoo, Binnaway, Baradine and Mendooran. 
With a rich history and stunning landscapes including spectacular mountain ranges, waterfalls, ancient sandstone caves, gorges, and beautiful plains, our scenic location amongst friendly country communities provides an ideal setting for those looking to balance a country lifestyle and career. 
At Warrumbungle Shire Council we offer a broad variety of jobs with a range of benefits and career development opportunities within Local Government. The guiding principles of honesty, integrity, fairness and compassion form the spirit of the team along with respect, transparency, passion, trust and opportunity is how Warrumbungle Shire Council strengthens its working environment to deliver on the aspirations of our community. 
Council is proud to be an equal opportunity and child safe employer with a commitment to our staff, and our vision is Excellence in Local Government. 
How to apply
Please provide sufficient detail in your answers to the questions as this information is used to assess your suitability for interview.

You will receive an email acknowledgement to confirm receipt of your application. You will receive email notifications regarding the status of your application. It is important that you regularly check your email to ensure you do not miss any notifications from Council. It is also recommended that you check your spam or junk folder and consider adding careers@warrumbungle.nsw.gov.au to your email address book to ensure you do not miss any correspondence in regard to your application.
Council's normal practice is to appoint at the entry salary for the grade. A higher commencing salary may be approved where an applicant can demonstrate significant directly relevant qualifications, skills and experience.

The MJH Group (incorporating the iconic McDonald Jones Homes and MOJO Homes brands) is not just in the new home building industry; we are in the business of delivering an unbeatable customer experience from beginning to end. We are proud to belong to the NEX Building Group, a diverse and expanding organisation with over 1300 passionate employees whose purpose is to build beautiful homes for Australians. Established in 1987 and continuing to evolve both organically and through acquisition, we are well positioned for growth and committed to achieving our vision of being Australia's leading home builder. 
Building new homes and better futures for Australians is a true honour and so rewarding. Here are some other rewards and benefits we offer our employees.
Our perks and benefits
We believe that our employee community is a key strength of our organisation, and we aim to attract the best talent to achieve our strategic goal of being Australia's leading residential builder and employer of choice in our sector. We are committed to taking care of our employees, that's why we offer a bundle of benefits:

- A genuine focus on diversity and inclusion (we're proud of our Women in Construction Program and annual Building Inclusivity Awards)

- A huge catalogue of online learning and ongoing professional development programs
- NAWIC and HIA corporate membership 
- Attractive remuneration
- And so much more!
About the opportunity
Reporting to the Drafting Team Leader and part of the MJH Drafting team, the key focus of this role is to ensure CAD drawings are accurately completed to reflect the customer requirements in a timely manner, and in accordance with current building regulations, company standards and procedures. More specifically, you will:
This full time role is a 12 month parental leave cover - with the possibility of extension

Interested?

candidates.content_text:
WE'RE HIRING
Building Cadet
Sunshine Coast, QLD | Full-Time or Part-Time (flexible around study)
This Isn't a Fetch-the-Coffee Cadetship
We're looking for a cadet who actually wants to learn how construction gets delivered.
Not someone waiting to be given a filing job. Someone curious, willing to ask questions, and ready to get involved from day one.
At Plexxcon, you'll work alongside our Project Managers, Contracts Administrators and Site Teams on live projects — learning how a job is planned, procured, programmed and built. You'll be in the thick of delivery, not watching it from a distance. From there you'll grow with clear pathways into Contracts Administration, Project Management or Site Management.
We deliver complex construction projects from $250K to $15M across Southeast Queensland, working inside live operational environments — hospitals, universities, schools, retail centres, sports clubs, industrial facilities and high-end commercial spaces.
Our clients don't stop operating while we build. That means communication matters. Planning matters. Relationships matter. Every decision has an impact.
It's a demanding place to learn. It's also the fastest way to learn properly.
What You'll Get
Real Exposure, Not Admin
You'll work on live projects from start-up through to handover. Programmes, procurement, subcontractor coordination, RFIs, variations, site inspections, progress reporting and client meetings. You'll see how the decisions made in week one show up in week thirty — and why a well-run project feels calm while a poorly-planned one never does.
Time on Site
You'll get out of the office regularly. Walking sites with our Site Managers, watching trades sequence, understanding what's actually achievable versus what looks fine on a programme. You can't learn this part from a textbook.
Mentorship From People Who Want You to Succeed
You'll be taught by experienced Project Managers, Contracts Administrators and Site Managers who've delivered hundreds of projects between them. Our leadership team is accessible and hands-on. Ask questions — you'll get answers.
Flexibility Around Your Study
Your degree matters. We'll structure your hours around your commitments, not the other way around. Plenty of our people have done exactly this.
A Clear Career Path
This isn't a dead-end role. We'll build your development around your strengths, with in-house upskilling and annual performance and development reviews where we talk openly about where you're heading, what you want to learn, and what's next. As Plexxcon grows, we want our people to grow with us.
A Team and Culture You'll Actually Enjoy
We're serious about performance and equally serious about building a workplace people want to be part of. Our values drive everything we do:
Relationships – We value strong relationships with our clients, subcontractors, suppliers and each other. Construction is a people business and we never lose sight of that.
Hustle – We move quickly, take ownership, and don't wait to be told what needs to be done.
Solutions – Complex projects require smart thinking, collaboration and problem solving, not finger-pointing.
Provide Value – We deliver quality outcomes that make commercial sense.
Bi-monthly team BBQs, social events throughout the year and a leadership team genuinely involved in the day-to-day. You'll know everyone's name in your first week.
What You'll Be Doing
- Supporting Project Managers and Contracts Administrators across live projects
- Preparing project start-up documentation — safety documents, ITPs, site set-up packs
- Assisting with procurement — scoping packages, raising purchase orders and subcontracts
- Reviewing drawings, specifications and consultant documentation
- Helping track programmes, progress claims and project reporting
- Managing RFIs, submittals and document control
- Attending site visits, site meetings and client meetings
- Coordinating with subcontractors, suppliers and consultants on day-to-day delivery
- Learning how projects are handed over — defects, O&M manuals, close-out
Who We're Looking For
✓ Currently studying or recently completed Construction Management, Civil Engineering or a related degree
✓ Genuinely interested in building a long-term career in commercial construction
✓ Strong attention to detail — in this industry, the details are the job
✓ Asks questions, puts their hand up, and gets involved

Tier 1 projects. Hands-on experience. Genuine career progression.
KeyBuild Services is a family-owned construction company delivering a diverse range of construction packages across major Tier 1 projects throughout South-East Queensland.
We are looking for a Construction Cadet who wants more than simply observing projects from the sidelines.
This role offers genuine hands-on experience across the construction lifecycle, working directly with our estimating, project and management teams to help coordinate and deliver multiple live projects.
The opportunity :
As your experience develops, you'll gain exposure across:
- Estimating, tendering and take-offs
- Design coordination and RFIs
- Procurement and subcontractor engagement
- Contracts, variations and cost management
- Programming and project coordination
- Site delivery and client interaction

Backed by Sumitomo Forestry Australia (one of the largest logging and processing companies worldwide), and part of the largest residential building group in Australia, we pride ourselves on delivering outstanding service and innovative solutions.

candidates.content_text:
About BMD
BMD is Australia's leading integrated engineering, construction and urban development business. As the largest privately owned civil contractor in Australia, BMD is at the forefront of excellence.
Over a 45-year history, BMD has grown to become a $2 billion operation, now sharing our expertise internationally in the Philippines and the UK.
About the Project
The Tram to Springvale Alliance (TSA), made up of BMD Constructions, CPB Contractors and Arup, is delivering the Eastern Freeway Upgrades between Tram and Springvale roads. The works include new express lanes, upgraded noise walls, and revitalised areas of the Koonung Creek Linear Park.
The project is being delivered under an Alliance Contract with Victorian Infrastructure Delivery Authority (VIDA), forming a single, collaborative team.  As part of the North East Link Program (NELP), the upgrade will improve safety and efficiency for over 135,000 daily vehicles, remove 15,000 trucks from local roads, and reduce traffic across the Yarra River by 50,000 vehicles per day.
We’re completing the link together and bringing it home for our community.
About the Role
We’re seeking a motivated Sustainability Graduate to join the TSA team. Reporting to the Land, Planning & Environment Manager, you’ll work closely with project stakeholders, consultants and delivery teams to support sustainability outcomes across the project.
Key Responsibilities
- Assist in delivering the project's sustainability strategy, objectives and reporting requirements
- Support sustainability performance monitoring, data collection and KPI reporting
- Contribute to sustainability initiatives that drive positive environmental, social and economic outcomes
- Help promote sustainability awareness and best practice across project teams
- Assist with compliance requirements, audits and sustainability documentation
- Collaborate with internal and external stakeholders to achieve project sustainability targets and support continuous improvement initiatives
What We’re Looking For
- Recently completed a degree in Sustainability, Environmental Science, Engineering or a related discipline
- Understanding of sustainability principles, legislation, guidelines and reporting frameworks
- Strong analytical and organisational skills with excellent attention to detail
- Effective communication and teamwork skills with a collaborative approach to problem-solving
- A genuine passion for sustainability and delivering positive project outcomes
What We Offer
- Be part of a nationally respected contractor with a strong local presence
- Benefit from job security, competitive salary, and long-term project pipelines
- Clear career progression and ongoing professional development
- Collaborate with top-tier delivery partners in a high-impact alliance
- Exposure to one of Victoria's largest transport infrastructure projects
- Be recognised at our annual employee awards event and through our Thrive reward and recognition platform
- Access wellness programs, strong work-life balance initiatives, paid parental leave, retail discounts, industry training and memberships & more
Ready to make a sustainable impact?
Apply now and be part of delivering better infrastructure and sustainable outcomes for Victoria through the North East Link Project.
We recognise that we are strengthened by diversity, and we embrace differences as an equal opportunity employer providing a flexible and inclusive workplace.
For further details on what makes BMD unique, head to https://www.bmdgroup.global

candidates.content_text:
Be the person who turns great designs into buildable homes
Todd Devine Homes is looking for a highly organised, proactive and solutions-focused Draftsperson to join our growing Design & Drafting team.
This role is ideal for an experienced residential drafting professional who enjoys more than simply producing drawings. You'll play a key role in translating concepts into practical, buildable solutions while coordinating information across design, estimating, sales and construction teams.
You'll work closely with our Development & Design Manager, Estimating, Sales, Construction teams and external consultants to ensure projects are documented accurately, efficiently and ready to progress through approvals and into construction.
If you're the kind of person who enjoys problem-solving, takes ownership of your work and wants the opportunity to grow with a business that's continually evolving, this could be a great fit.
About the role
As our Draftsperson, you'll take ownership of project documentation from concept design through to construction-ready drawings.
Your role will include:
- Preparing and maintaining residential working drawings and construction documentation
- Developing buildable drafting solutions for custom homes, modular housing and Small Second Dwellings
- Producing sales, permit, tender and construction documentation packages
- Modifying and adapting standard plans to suit client requirements, site constraints and project objectives
- Coordinating and incorporating information from engineers, surveyors, energy assessors and other consultants
- Preparing and managing documentation required for planning, building permits and approvals
- Reviewing plans for compliance with the NCC, Victorian Building Regulations and relevant planning requirements
- Assisting with ResCode and planning-related documentation where required
- Working closely with Estimating to ensure documentation aligns with project scope and budgets
- Liaising with Sales and Pre-Construction teams to resolve design, compliance and constructability queries
- Managing drawing revisions and maintaining accurate project documentation records
- Updating project information and documentation within ClickHome and related systems
- Identifying design clashes, construction risks and documentation issues before they impact delivery
- Supporting continuous improvement of drafting standards, templates and documentation processes
- Contributing ideas and solutions that improve efficiency, buildability and customer outcomes
What you'll bring
We're looking for someone who combines strong technical drafting capability with practical thinking and a proactive approach to problem-solving.
You'll ideally have:
- Experience working within a custom residential building environment
- Strong proficiency in Revit, with AutoCAD experience also regarded
- A solid understanding of residential construction methods and building systems
- Knowledge of the National Construction Code (NCC), Victorian Building Regulations and residential design requirements
- Experience preparing working drawings, permit documentation and construction documentation
- Confidence coordinating consultant information and resolving documentation issues
- Excellent attention to detail and commitment to producing accurate documentation
- Strong organisational skills and the ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously
- The ability to identify problems, think critically and develop practical solutions
- Strong communication skills and confidence working with internal teams, consultants and stakeholders
- A collaborative approach and willingness to contribute across different areas of the business
- A genuine desire to learn, improve and grow with the company
Experience with modular, prefabricated or off-site construction methods would be highly regarded, but is not essential.
What success looks like
You'll know you're succeeding when:
- Drawings are accurate, coordinated and ready for construction with minimal rework
- Consultants, estimators and construction teams can rely on the quality of your documentation
- Design and compliance issues are identified and resolved early in the process
- Projects progress smoothly through approvals and into construction
- Documentation standards remain consistent across all project types
- Opportunities to improve buildability and efficiency are regularly identified
- Internal teams value your contribution as a trusted technical and problem-solving resource
- You continue developing your skills and take on increasing responsibility as the business grows
About Todd Devine Homes
Todd Devine Homes is an established Victorian home builder specialising in modern prefabricated and residential housing solutions.
We work across a diverse range of projects, from individual homes and Small Second Dwellings through to multi-home developments, lifestyle communities and commercial accommodation projects.
Our team brings together sales, design, estimating, construction and operations, giving this role the opportunity to work across multiple areas of the business and gain a strong understanding of the complete home-building journey.
As our business grows, we are committed to creating opportunities for our people to broaden their skills, contribute new ideas and grow alongside the company.
The details
Location: Bayswater, VIC
Employment: Full-time
Reports to: Development & Design Manager
